definition_zh: 生计；谋生之道；收入来源
definition_en: the way a person earns money to live, or the money that keeps a person or group alive
core_image: 渔夫清晨收网，一网鱼就是一家人全年的活命钱
scene: 小海村里，捕鱼和晒盐就是家家户户的活命收入。In the small fishing village, catching fish and drying salt were the livelihood of every household.
sceneCN: 这里 livelihood 是「生计、谋生之道」（第 1 个义项：靠什么活下来的收入来源）；句意：在这个小渔村里，捕鱼和晒盐就是每家每户的生计。

pos.zh: 生计；谋生之道；收入来源

derivatives.zh: live 加 -ing 构成，义为「生活；生计」，如 earn a living
live 加 -ly 构成，义为「活泼的；有生气的」，与 livelihood 同源但意思转向
life 加 long 构成，义为「终身的」，与 livelihood 共享 life 这一成分

senses.title: The way someone earns a living
senses.definition: the way in which a person earns money to support life
senses.definitionCN: 一个人挣钱维持生活的方式
senses.example: Fishing is the livelihood of many coastal families.
senses.exampleCN: 捕鱼是许多沿海家庭的生计。
senses.why: Livelihood joins life with a word for path, so a way of earning is literally the path by which life is kept going.
senses.whyCN: livelihood 把「生命」和「道路」组合在一起，所以谋生之道就是让生命延续的那条路。

senses.title: The money or means of support
senses.definition: the income or means of support that keeps a person alive
senses.definitionCN: 维持一个人活下去的收入或生活来源
senses.example: The drought destroyed the livelihood of entire villages.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱毁掉了整个村庄的生活来源。
senses.why: The path of life can be the supply that feeds it, so the word also names the means or money that keeps a person alive.
senses.whyCN: 生命的道路也可以指供给生命的东西，所以这个词也指维持生命的财物与收入。

senses.title: A job as a source of income
senses.definition: a job or occupation that provides a steady income
senses.definitionCN: 提供稳定收入的工作或职业
senses.example: Mining was his livelihood for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 采矿是他三十年的饭碗。
senses.why: The path of life is most often a trade, so a job that supplies money becomes the concrete form of the word.
senses.whyCN: 生命的道路往往就是一门手艺，所以提供收入的工作成为这个词的具体形态。

senses.title: The traditional way of life of a community
senses.definition: the customary activity by which a whole community supports itself
senses.definitionCN: 整个社区赖以维生的传统活动
senses.example: Farming remains a key element of the local livelihood.
senses.exampleCN: 农业仍然是当地谋生方式的重要一项。
senses.why: A whole community shares one path of survival, so the word widens from one person to the trade of a place.
senses.whyCN: 整个社区共享同一条活路，所以这个词从一个人扩展到一地的产业。

senses.title: A means of survival in hard times
senses.definition: something relied on to keep body and soul together when times are hard
senses.definitionCN: 艰难时期赖以糊口的东西
senses.example: For many, the small shop is a livelihood of last resort.
senses.exampleCN: 对许多人来说，这家小店是最后的糊口之计。
senses.why: When the usual path is hard, any small supply becomes the path, and the word takes on a sense of scraping by.
senses.whyCN: 当正常的路难走时，任何微小的来源都成了一条活路，于是有了勉强度日的意思。

senses.title: Protection of a way of earning
senses.definition: the legal or social protection of one ability to earn money
senses.definitionCN: 对一个人挣钱能力的法律或社会保护
senses.example: The law protects the livelihood of street vendors.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法律保护街头摊贩的生计。
senses.why: Law and public policy treat the path of earning as something a person may be protected in following.
senses.whyCN: 法律与公共政策把谋生之路看作一个人可以受到保护去走的路。

senses.title: A family asset kept for future support
senses.definition: a property or resource kept to support a household in future
senses.definitionCN: 为将来支撑家庭而保留的田产或资源
senses.example: The old mill was a livelihood the family had kept for generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老磨坊是这家人几代相传、用来养家的田产。
senses.why: A property that feeds a family is a path held for the future, an older use that survives in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 养活一家人的产业是一条为将来保留的活路，这是仍见于正式文字中的旧用法。

senses.title: The wages on which workers depend
senses.definition: the pay on which workers and their families depend, especially in public debate
senses.definitionCN: 工人及其家人所依赖的工资，尤见于公共讨论
senses.example: The strike was over wages on which livelihoods depended.
senses.exampleCN: 这次罢工源于工人们赖以为生的工资。
senses.why: Wages are the most direct path from work to life, so the word appears in disputes over pay.
senses.whyCN: 工资是从劳动通向生活最直接的路，所以这个词出现在关于报酬的争议中。

intro.en: Livelihood joins the old English noun by which meant life with the word lode, meaning a way or course, from the Old English liflad, a way of life.
intro.cn: livelihood 由中古英语中表示「生命」的 liveli 与表示「道路、途径」的 lode 组合而成，可上溯到古英语 liflad（生活方式）。

items.en: Liflad combines lif, life, with lad, a course or leading, and means a way of life.
items.cn: liflad 由 lif（生命）和 lad（道路、引领）组合，意为生活方式。

items.en: The form shifts to lyflode and then livelode, still meaning way of life or means of living.
items.cn: 拼写先变为 lyflode，再变为 livelode，仍指生活方式或生活来源。

items.en: The second element is reshaped by spellings familiar from English words that clearly mean life and way.
items.cn: 词尾受表示「生命」与「方式」的熟悉拼写影响而改写。

items.en: Livelihood settles as a noun for the means of keeping alive and earning a living.
items.cn: livelihood 固定为表示「维持生活和谋生手段」的名词。

items.en: The word becomes standard in economics, law, and humanitarian language.
items.cn: 在现代英语中，这个词成为经济、法律和人道事务领域的标准用语。

note.en: Livelihood is a compound of live, and it sits close in meaning to living, income, and subsistence.
note.cn: livelihood 是 live 的复合形式，语义上接近 living、income 与 subsistence。

entries.definition: the quality of being full of energy
entries.definitionCN: 活泼；充满生气（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: the money needed to support life
entries.definitionCN: 生活；生计

entries.definition: full of energy and interest
entries.definitionCN: 活泼的；有生气的

entries.definition: money received, especially from work
entries.definitionCN: 收入

entries.definition: the state of having just enough food and money to stay alive
entries.definitionCN: 勉强糊口；生存

entries.definition: a person regular job
entries.definitionCN: 职业

normalIntro.en: Read livelihood as the live plus the way, the route by which a person keeps life going.
normalIntro.cn: 把 livelihood 读作 life 加 way：一个人维持生命的道路。

normal.en: To lose a livelihood means to lose the way of earning money.
normal.cn: lose a livelihood 指失去谋生的办法。

normal.en: Earn a livelihood is the formal twin of earn a living.
normal.cn: earn a livelihood 是 earn a living 的正式说法。

normal.en: Fishermen, farmers, and miners all have a livelihood tied to land and sea.
normal.cn: 渔夫、农夫和矿工的生计都系于土地与海洋。

normal.en: Means of livelihood appears in news reports about lost jobs.
normal.cn: means of livelihood 常见于失业新闻的报道中。

normal.en: Compare living: living is shorter and everyday, livelihood is more formal and social.
normal.cn: 对比 living：living 更短更日常，livelihood 更正式、更偏社会议题。

abstract.en: Picture a fisherman hauling in the net at dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象天刚亮时渔夫把网拉上岸。

abstract.en: Picture a shop on a crowded street that feeds a whole family.
abstract.cn: 想象闹市里一家养活全家的小店。

abstract.en: Picture a map line from home to workplace that must never be cut.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从家通向工作地、绝不能被切断的线。

examples.en: The new road threatens the livelihood of local farmers.
examples.cn: 这条新路威胁着当地农民的生计。

examples.en: Many villagers lost their livelihoods when the factory closed.
examples.cn: 工厂关闭后，许多村民失去了生计。

examples.en: Tourism has become the main livelihood of the old town.
examples.cn: 旅游业已成为这座古城的谋生之道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读音「赖福利」——一个人「赖」着工作那点「福利」活命，就是生计；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 lif（生命）+ lad（道路、引导）→ liflad（生活方式）→ 中古英语 livelode → livelihood：生命的道路，即「活命的路子」。

sensesIntro.en: Livelihood is a way of life narrowed into the means of keeping alive, first a general way of earning, then a community norm, then a term of law and social debate.
sensesIntro.cn: livelihood 从「生活方式」窄化为「活命的手段」，先指一般谋生方式，再指群体的传统生计，最后成为法律与社会议题的术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fisherman drawing a full net at dawn.
core.cn: 核心意象：渔夫在晨光中拉起满网的鱼。

branches.en: The general way of earning a living is the core sense.
branches.cn: 一般性的谋生方式是核心义项。

branches.en: The money that keeps a person alive is the support sense.
branches.cn: 维持生命的钱是「生活来源」义项。

branches.en: A steady job is the occupational sense.
branches.cn: 稳定的工作是职业义项。

branches.en: A community way of earning and a last resort in hard times are social and survival branches.
branches.cn: 群体谋生方式与艰难时的糊口之计，是社会与生存两条分支。

branches.en: Protected livelihoods and dependent wages belong to law and labour debate.
branches.cn: 受保护的生计与赖以维生的工资属于法律与劳工议题。

intro.en: Livelihood is a native English compound of life and a word for way, and living and lively are its best known relatives.
intro.cn: livelihood 是英语本土的复合词，由 life 和表示「道路」的词合成，最近的亲属是 living 与 lively。

latinIntro.en: Livelihood is native English with no Latin ancestor, though the Latin verb vivere, to live, is a distant cousin.
latinIntro.cn: livelihood 是英语本土词，没有拉丁语祖先，不过拉丁语 vivere（生活）是远亲。

items.example: Lif opens the first half of the word.
items.exampleCN: lif 构成这个词的前半部分。

items.example: Lad supplies the sense of a course or way.
items.exampleCN: lad 提供「道路、途径」的意思。

items.example: Liflad is the oldest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: liflad 是有记录的最早形式。

items.example: Livelode is the Middle English stage.
items.exampleCN: livelode 是中古英语阶段的形式。

items.example: Live shares the first element of livelihood.
items.exampleCN: live 与 livelihood 共享第一部分。

items.example: Living is the everyday twin of livelihood.
items.exampleCN: living 是 livelihood 的日常同义形式。

items.example: Lively keeps the life element in another branch.
items.exampleCN: lively 在另一条分支上保留了 life 的成分。

items.example: The ending recalls the -hood of childhood and brotherhood.
items.exampleCN: 词尾让人联想到 childhood、brotherhood 中的 -hood。

items.example: Livelihoods is the regular plural.
items.exampleCN: livelihoods 是规则的复数形式。

definition_zh: 蜥蜴；有鳞四足爬行动物；皮制小袋；一小撮头发
definition_en: a small reptile with a long tail and four legs that moves quickly on the ground
core_image: 一只小蜥蜴趴在晒烫的石头上，转眼钻进石缝里
scene: 午后的石墙上，一只小蜥蜴一动不动地晒着太阳，尾巴上有一道亮黄。On the stone wall at midday, a small lizard hung quite still in the sun, with a bright yellow stripe down its tail.
sceneCN: 这里 lizard 是「蜥蜴」（第 1 个义项：有长尾和四肢的小型爬行动物）；句意：正午时分，石墙上一只小蜥蜴一动不动地晒太阳，尾巴上有一道亮黄色。

pos.zh: 蜥蜴；蜥蜴类爬行动物；皮小袋；一小撮头发

collocations.phrase: a lizard basking on a rock
collocations.zh: 在石头上晒太阳的蜥蜴

derivatives.zh: lizard 加 -like 构成，义为「似蜥蜴的」
lizard 加 -ry 构成，多用于园艺与自然写作，义为「蜥蜴类动物」
lizard 的规则复数形式，指「多只蜥蜴」

senses.title: A small four legged reptile
senses.definition: a small reptile with four legs and a long tail, usually covered in scales
senses.definitionCN: 有四肢和长尾、通常覆有鳞片的小型爬行动物
senses.example: A lizard darted across the path and vanished into the grass.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蜥蜴窜过小路，消失在草丛里。
senses.why: The English word has named this scaly four legged animal since the fourteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 英语里这个词从十四世纪起就指这种有鳞片的四足动物。

senses.title: Any member of the lizard group
senses.definition: any reptile of the group that includes iguanas, geckos, and monitors
senses.definitionCN: 包括鬣蜥、壁虎和巨蜥在内的蜥蜴类爬行动物
senses.example: Geckos are lizards that can climb smooth glass.
senses.exampleCN: 壁虎是能够攀爬光滑玻璃的蜥蜴。
senses.why: Biology widened the everyday animal name into a class name, even when the animal is called a gecko or a skink.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把这个日常动物名扩展为类名，即使该动物被叫作壁虎或石龙子。

senses.title: A leather bag worn at a belt in Scottish use
senses.definition: a small leather pouch hung from a belt, used in the Scottish Highlands
senses.definitionCN: 苏格兰高地人挂在腰带上的一种皮制小袋
senses.example: The piper carried his silver spoon in the lizard.
senses.exampleCN: 风笛手把银勺装在小皮袋里。
senses.why: This unrelated sense, a pouch at the belt, comes through Old French and Latin aluta, softened leather, rather than the animal word.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项与动物无关，指腰间的皮袋，经古法语上溯到拉丁语 aluta（鞣软的皮革）。

senses.title: A short strand of hair tied at the side in dialect use
senses.definition: a short strand of hair tied at the side of the head, recorded in dialect use
senses.definitionCN: 方言中记录的在头侧扎起的一小撮头发
senses.example: In northern dialect the woman wore a lizard behind her ear.
senses.exampleCN: 在北方方言中，那位女士在耳后扎了一小撮头发。
senses.why: Dialect records a rare sense in which the word names a small tied strand of hair, now archaic.
senses.whyCN: 方言中记录了一个罕见的义项，指扎起来的一小撮头发，现已古旧。

senses.title: Something shaped like a lizard
senses.definition: a thing or ornament shaped to resemble a lizard
senses.definitionCN: 外形或装饰做成蜥蜴样子的物件
senses.example: He wore a gold lizard as a tie pin.
senses.exampleCN: 他戴着一枚金蜥蜴形状的领带针。
senses.why: Like many animal names, the word can label a thing whose shape copies the animal.
senses.whyCN: 与许多动物名称一样，这个词也可以指外形模仿该动物的物件。

senses.title: Leather made from lizard skin
senses.definition: leather or a product made from the skin of a lizard
senses.definitionCN: 用蜥蜴皮制成的皮革或皮制品
senses.example: Her purse was made of lizard.
senses.exampleCN: 她的手袋是蜥蜴皮做的。
senses.why: A material noun grows from the animal name when the skin itself becomes a product.
senses.whyCN: 当动物皮本身成为一种产品时，动物名就引申为表示材料的物质名词。

senses.title: A fishing lure shaped like a lizard
senses.definition: an artificial bait for fish that is shaped like a lizard
senses.definitionCN: 做成蜥蜴样子、用来钓鱼的人造鱼饵
senses.example: He tied a plastic lizard onto the hook.
senses.exampleCN: 他把一只塑料蜥蜴系在鱼钩上。
senses.why: Anglers name soft baits after the creatures they imitate, so the lizard name spreads to bait.
senses.whyCN: 钓鱼人常以所模仿的生物给软饵命名，于是蜥蜴这个名字也用于鱼饵。

senses.title: A person who is quick and hard to catch
senses.definition: an informal way to describe a person who is quick, slippery, or hard to catch
senses.definitionCN: 口语中形容反应快、滑溜、难以抓到手的人
senses.example: That little lizard slipped out of the interview in a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 那个滑溜的家伙一分钟就从面试里溜走了。
senses.why: The animal quick darting image is transferred to a person who is hard to hold down.
senses.whyCN: 蜥蜴倏忽钻走的画面被移用到难以拿捏的人身上。

intro.en: Lizard comes through Old French from Latin lacerta, with the middle sound changed under the influence of heraldry and everyday speech.
intro.cn: lizard 经古法语的旧形式上溯到拉丁语 lacerta（蜥蜴），中间的音在纹章用语和日常口语影响下发生了变化。

items.en: Lacerta is the Latin name of the lizard, the same word that names the constellation.
items.cn: lacerta 是拉丁语对蜥蜴的称呼，星座名也沿用此词。

items.en: The Latin word passes into Old French as lesard(e), with the k sound dropped.
items.cn: 该拉丁词进入古法语时作 lesard(e)，其中的 k 音脱落。

items.en: English adopts the word around the fourteenth century as lesard or leserde.
items.cn: 英语约在十四世纪以 lesard 或 leserde 的形式借入。

items.en: The spelling settles as lizard, probably helped by heraldic French forms of the word.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 lizard，可能受到法语纹章用语中该词写法的影响。

items.en: The word becomes the standard everyday and scientific name for the scaly reptile.
items.cn: 在现代英语中，这个词成为这种有鳞爬行动物的日常与学术标准名。

note.en: Lizard is one Latin-reared reptile name, close in spelling toizzard and wizard and in meaning to gecko, skink, and salamander.
note.cn: lizard 是源自拉丁语的爬行动物名，拼写上接近izzard 与 wizard，意义上接近 gecko、skink 与 salamander。

entries.definition: a man with magic powers in fairy stories
entries.definitionCN: 巫师（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: an old name for the letter z
entries.definitionCN: 字母 z 的旧称（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: more than one lizard
entries.definitionCN: 多只蜥蜴

entries.definition: a small lizard with pads on its toes that can climb walls
entries.definitionCN: 脚趾有吸盘、能爬墙的小蜥蜴

entries.definition: a smooth shiny lizard found in warm regions
entries.definitionCN: 生活在温暖地区的石龙子

entries.definition: a small animal like a lizard that lives near water
entries.definitionCN: 形似蜥蜴、生活在水边的小动物

normalIntro.en: Lizard keeps the Latin sounds of lacerta but loses the k in French, and gecko and skink are its smaller cousins in name.
normalIntro.cn: lizard 保留了拉丁语 lacerta 的大部分音，却在法语里丢掉了 k 音；而 gecko、skink 是它名字上的小表亲。

normal.en: A lizard is one of many lizards, so the plural is simply lizards.
normal.cn: 一只 lizard 是众多 lizards 中的一只，复数直接加 s。

normal.en: Lizard skin is worked into purses and shoes.
normal.cn: 蜥蜴皮被制成手袋和鞋子。

normal.en: Gecko and skink are specific lizards with their own names.
normal.cn: 壁虎和石龙子都是各有名字的特定蜥蜴。

normal.en: Do not confuse lizard with wizard, a man of magic in tales.
normal.cn: 不要把 lizard 与 wizard 混淆，后者是故事里的巫师。

normal.en: Lacerta is the Latin lizard and also the name of a constellation.
normal.cn: lacerta 是拉丁语的蜥蜴，也是一个星座的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a gecko frozen on a hot stone, then gone in a flick.
abstract.cn: 想象一只壁虎在晒烫的石头上静止不动，一闪就消失。

abstract.en: Picture a whole wall of small scaled cousins, each with its own name.
abstract.cn: 想象一整面墙的小鳞片表亲，每一只都有自己的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a belt pouch hanging like a small scaled animal.
abstract.cn: 想象腰间挂着一只皮袋，像一只盘着的小动物。

examples.en: The little lizard froze when we came closer.
examples.cn: 我们走近时，那只小蜥蜴一动不动。

examples.en: Desert lizards can survive for weeks without drinking water.
examples.cn: 沙漠里的蜥蜴可以数周不喝水而活下来。

examples.en: Lizards and snakes both have scales and shed their skin.
examples.cn: 蜥蜴和蛇都有鳞片，也都会蜕皮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读音「里泽德」——「里」屋石头缝「泽」边，一只小「德」性蜥蜴钻来钻去；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 lacerta（蜥蜴）→ 古法语 lesard(e) → 中古英语 lesard / leserde → 现代英语 lizard（中间音受纹章用语影响而改写，词根无争议）。

sensesIntro.en: Lizard starts as the everyday name of a scaly four legged reptile, widens into its scientific class, and then spreads to things shaped like it or made from it.
sensesIntro.cn: lizard 最初是有鳞四足爬行动物的日常名，后来扩展为科学的类名，再延伸到形状或材质像它的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small lizard sunning itself, ready to dart away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只晒太阳的小蜥蜴，随时准备一窜而走。

branches.en: The small four legged reptile is the core sense.
branches.cn: 小型四足爬行动物是核心义项。

branches.en: The whole family of scaly climbers is the biological sense.
branches.cn: 整个有鳞攀爬动物家族是生物学义项。

branches.en: A belt pouch comes from a different Latin word, aluta, and is a homograph rather than a meaning branch.
branches.cn: 腰间的皮袋来自另一个拉丁词 aluta，属同形异源，而非语义分支。

branches.en: A tied strand of hair and a slippery person are both rare or informal extensions.
branches.cn: 扎起的一撮头发与滑溜的人，都是罕见或口语的延伸。

branches.en: Ornaments, leather, and fish lures all take the animal shape or skin.
branches.cn: 饰品、皮革与鱼饵都借用了蜥蜴的形状或皮料。

intro.en: Lizard is a whole borrowing of the Latin animal name, and English adds -like and -ry to build new words from it.
intro.cn: lizard 是整体借用拉丁语动物名而来的词，英语再用 -like、-ry 在其上构词。

latinIntro.en: Latin lacerta is both the lizard and its name, and it passes into French and then English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lacerta 既是蜥蜴本身，也是它的名字，经法语进入英语。

items.example: Lacerta gives the word its root sense.
items.exampleCN: lacerta 提供这个词的词根含义。

items.example: Lesard(e) drops the k sound of the Latin form.
items.exampleCN: lesard(e) 丢掉了拉丁形式的 k 音。

items.example: Lizard is the standard modern name.
items.exampleCN: lizard 是现代标准名称。

items.example: The suffix -like forms lizardlike.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -like 构成 lizardlike。

items.example: Lizardlike describes a quick, scaled appearance.
items.exampleCN: lizardlike 形容有鳞片、动作快的模样。

items.meaningCN: 表示类别或集合的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ry forms lizardry.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ry 构成 lizardry。

items.example: Lizardry names lizards as a group.
items.exampleCN: lizardry 把蜥蜴作为一个类别来称呼。

items.example: The suffix -s forms lizards.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 lizards。

items.meaning: the skin of a lizard, used as leather
items.example: Lizard skin appears in shoe making.
items.exampleCN: 蜥蜴皮见于制鞋业。

definition_zh: 不愿意的；不情愿的；厌恶的
definition_en: unwilling or reluctant to do something
core_image: 一个人站在门口，手抵着门框，迟迟不肯迈进去
scene: 主人再三邀请他上台唱一首，他只是摇头，怎么也不肯挪动半步。The guest was loath to sing at the party, so he stayed in his seat.
sceneCN: 这里 loath 是「不情愿的」（第 1 个义项：不愿做某事）；句意：这位客人不情愿在聚会上唱歌，所以一直坐在座位上。

pos.zh: 厌恶的；讨厌的（多见于书面语，与 of 连用）

derivatives.zh: 古旧副词：不情愿地；也可作形容词，意为「可厌的」
由 loath 加 -ness 构成，义为「不情愿；厌恶」
由 loath 加 -some 构成，义为「令人厌恶的」
loath 的常见异体拼写，含义完全相同

senses.title: Reluctant to act
senses.definition: unwilling or reluctant to do something
senses.definitionCN: 不愿意或勉强去做某事
senses.example: She was loath to leave the warm room.
senses.exampleCN: 她不愿意离开温暖的房间。
senses.why: In Old English the word meant hateful or hostile, so to be loath is to feel that an action is against your will.
senses.whyCN: 在古英语中这个词本义是「可恨的、敌对的」，所以 loath 就是觉得某个动作违背自己的心意。

senses.title: Disgusted by something
senses.definition: feeling disgust or strong dislike towards someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某事物感到厌恶或强烈反感
senses.example: He is loath of violence in any form.
senses.exampleCN: 他厌恶任何形式的暴力。
senses.why: The older sense of loath is hateful, describing something you find disgusting, a sense still kept in literary English with of.
senses.whyCN: loath 更古老的含义是「可恨的」，用来形容让人觉得恶心的东西，书面语中与 of 连用的这个义项保留至今。

senses.title: Uttered with reluctance
senses.titleCN: 勉强的（修饰话语或承认）
senses.definition: used of words or admissions that are forced out unwillingly
senses.definitionCN: 用于勉强说出口的话语或承认
senses.example: With a loath apology, the driver gave way.
senses.exampleCN: 司机不情不愿地道了歉，然后让开了路。
senses.why: Reluctance moves from the person to the words, so a loath remark is one dragged out against the will.
senses.whyCN: 不情愿从人身上转移到话语上，于是「loath 的说法」就是被迫挤出来、违背本意的话。

senses.title: Nothing loath
senses.definition: a set phrase meaning very willing indeed
senses.definitionCN: 固定说法，意为其实非常乐意、毫不推辞
senses.example: Nothing loath, the children ran down to the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们毫不推辞，立刻跑向海边。
senses.why: A negated form flips the sense, and the double negative makes eager consent sound pleasingly understated.
senses.whyCN: 加了否定词之后语义反转，双重否定让「欣然答应」显得含蓄而有味道。

senses.title: Loath to part with
senses.definition: unwilling to separate from a person, place, or possession
senses.definitionCN: 不愿与人、地方或财物分离，难以放手
senses.example: The old man was loath to part with his tools.
senses.exampleCN: 老人舍不得放下他的这些工具。
senses.why: Reluctance turned towards an object becomes the regret of letting something precious go.
senses.whyCN: 不情愿的对象转向一件物品，就变成了放走珍贵东西时的不舍。

senses.title: Formal register
senses.definition: a somewhat literary and formal way of saying unwilling
senses.definitionCN: 较为书面、正式的「不愿意」表达方式
senses.example: The council is loath to set a firm date.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会不愿定下一个具体日期。
senses.why: Because the word survives mainly in written English, it signals a considered, formal kind of unwillingness.
senses.whyCN: 这个词主要存活于书面语，因此带有经过斟酌的正式语气，比日常的「不愿意」更显谨慎。

intro.en: Loath goes back to Old English lath, meaning hateful, and is related to the everyday verb loathe, to hate.
intro.cn: loath 源自意为「可恨的」的古英语 lath，与日常动词 loathe（憎恨）同源。

items.en: Lath means hateful, hostile, or unpleasant.
items.cn: 古英语 lath 意为可恨的、敌对的、令人不快的。

items.en: The senses hateful and unwilling already exist side by side.
items.cn: 「可恨的」与「不情愿的」两个义项当时已经并存。

items.en: Lath becomes loth, and the spelling loath spreads in later texts.
items.cn: 中古英语中 lath 写作 loth，稍后文本里 loath 的拼写逐渐流行。

items.en: The sense hateful fades, leaving unwilling as the main meaning.
items.cn: 「可恨的」义逐渐消退，「不情愿的」成为主要含义。

items.en: Loath and loathe split: the adjective stays loath, the verb becomes loathe.
items.cn: 形容词与动词分家：形容词写作 loath，动词写作 loathe。

note.en: Loath is the adjective of unwillingness, easily confused with the verb loathe, and it sits near reluctant, averse, and other refusal words.
note.cn: loath 是表示「不情愿」的形容词，容易与动词 loathe 混淆，语义上挨着 reluctant、averse 这一类「不愿」的表达。

entries.definition: to hate or detest something
entries.definitionCN: 憎恨；厌恶（动词，与 loath 同源，但词性与读音都不同）

entries.definition: an alternative spelling of loath
entries.definitionCN: loath 的异体拼写，含义相同

entries.definition: extremely unpleasant or disgusting
entries.definitionCN: 令人厌恶的；恶心的

entries.definition: unwilling and slow to agree
entries.definitionCN: 不情愿的；勉强的

entries.definition: having a strong dislike of something
entries.definitionCN: 厌恶的；反对的（常与 to 连用）

entries.definition: not willing or not inclined to do something
entries.definitionCN: 不愿意的；不乐意的

normalIntro.en: Loath is the adjective of unwillingness, and its brother loathe is the verb meaning to hate.
normalIntro.cn: loath 是表示「不愿意」的形容词，它的兄弟 loathe 才是表示「憎恨」的动词。

normal.en: The usual pattern is be loath to do something.
normal.cn: 常见结构是 be loath to do something，表示不情愿做某事。

normal.en: Reluctant and loath are close, but loath sounds more formal and literary.
normal.cn: reluctant 与 loath 意思接近，但 loath 更正式、更书面。

normal.en: Remember the pair: loath is the adjective, loathe with an e is the verb.
normal.cn: 记住这一对：loath 是形容词，带 e 的 loathe 是动词。

normal.en: Nothing loath is an old idiom meaning very willing.
normal.cn: nothing loath 是古老习语，意思是其实非常乐意。

normal.en: Loath to part with captures the feeling of not wanting to let something go.
normal.cn: loath to part with 形容舍不得放手的感觉。

abstract.en: Picture a person with one hand on the door frame, not stepping in.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人一只手扶着门框，迟迟不肯迈进去。

abstract.en: Imagine turning your face away from a dish you cannot stand.
abstract.cn: 想象你把脸从一道受不了的菜前面转开。

abstract.en: See a sentence being pushed out word by word, painfully slow.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话被一个字一个字地挤出来，慢得让人难受。

examples.en: I am loath to spend my whole weekend on this report.
examples.cn: 我不太愿意把整个周末都花在这份报告上。

examples.en: The committee was loath to approve the plan without more data.
examples.cn: 委员会不愿在没有更多数据的情况下批准这项计划。

examples.en: She was loath to admit that her first guess had been wrong.
examples.cn: 她不愿承认自己最初的猜测错了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「漏了丝」——好像哪里漏了一点丝线，心里犯嘀咕，于是不情愿动手；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 lath（可恨的、敌对的）→ 中古英语 loth → 现代英语 loath，核心义由「令人厌恶」转为「心里不愿」，同源动词为 loathe（憎恨）。

sensesIntro.en: Loath starts from an inner refusal to act, extends to disgust at a thing, and lives on in set phrases and formal writing.
sensesIntro.cn: loath 从内心拒绝行动出发，扩展到对某物的厌恶，并以固定说法和正式书面语的形式延续至今。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with one hand on the door frame, refusing to step in.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人手扶门框，就是不肯迈步进去。

branches.en: Reluctance to act is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 不愿行动是日常义项。

branches.en: Disgust keeps the old hateful sense.
branches.cn: 厌恶义保留了古老的可恨意味。

branches.en: A loath apology carries the reluctance into the words themselves.
branches.cn: loath 的道歉把不情愿带进了话语本身。

branches.en: Nothing loath reverses the sense into eager consent.
branches.cn: nothing loath 把词义反转为乐于答应。

branches.en: Not parting with things and formal usage extend the core refusal.
branches.cn: 舍不得放手与正式用法都是核心拒绝义的延伸。

intro.en: Loath is a native English adjective with no productive affixes, but it forms a small family with loathe, loathsome, loathness, and the old adverb loathly.
intro.cn: loath 是土生土长的英语形容词，本身没有能产的词缀，但围绕它形成了 loathe、loathsome、loathness 以及古老副词 loathly 这一小家族。

latinIntro.en: Loath has no Latin ancestor, since it comes from Old English lath, so there are no Latin cognates to list.
latinIntro.cn: loath 没有拉丁语祖先，它来自古英语 lath，因此没有可列的拉丁同源词。

items.example: Loath is the base adjective.
items.exampleCN: loath 是基础形容词。

items.example: The verb forms loathe from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 动词 loathe 由同一词干构成。

items.example: The suffix -some forms loathsome.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -some 构成 loathsome。

items.example: Loathsome describes something hateful.
items.exampleCN: loathsome 形容令人憎恶的事物。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms loathness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 loathness。

items.example: Loathness is the rare noun of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: loathness 是这个形容词罕见的名词形式。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the old adverb loathly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成古老的副词 loathly。

items.meaningCN: 不情愿地；也可作形容词，意为可厌的
items.example: Loathly survives mainly in older literature.
items.exampleCN: loathly 主要见于较古老的文学作品。

items.example: Loth is a common alternative spelling.
items.exampleCN: loth 是常见的异体拼写。

definition_zh: 龙虾；龙虾肉；龙虾色
definition_en: a large sea creature with a hard shell, ten legs, and two big front claws, eaten as food
core_image: 一只红壳龙虾在浅海礁石间，举着两只大钳子缓缓爬行
scene: 渔民从网里取出一只红壳大海鲜，挥着两只大钳子，孩子们围过来看。The fisherman pulled a lobster from the trap and held it up by its back.
sceneCN: 这里 lobster 是「龙虾」（第 1 个义项：有硬壳和大钳子的海生动物）；句意：渔民从笼子里掏出一只龙虾，捏着它的背把它举了起来。

pos.zh: 龙虾色的；橘红色的（多见于英国英语）

collocations.zh: 非正式说法：爱变色的花招（印度英语）

derivatives.zh: 由 lobster 与 man 复合而成，义为「捕龙虾的渔夫」
由 lobster 加 -ing 构成，义为「捕龙虾这件事」
由 lobster 加 -ish 构成，戏称「有龙虾味的；像龙虾一样红或笨拙的」

senses.title: The large sea animal
senses.definition: a large sea creature with a hard shell and strong front claws
senses.definitionCN: 有坚硬外壳和大前钳的海洋动物
senses.example: A lobster waved its antennae at the camera.
senses.exampleCN: 一只龙虾朝镜头挥着触须。
senses.why: The Old English name combined loppe, a spider, with the word for a plaited basket, because the creature looks like a spider in a woven cage.
senses.whyCN: 古英语名字由 loppe（蜘蛛）与「编织篮子」一词组合而成，因为这个生物就像困在编织笼子里的蜘蛛。

senses.title: The meat on a plate
senses.definition: the meat of this animal eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 作为食物食用的这种动物的肉
senses.example: We ordered lobster with garlic butter.
senses.exampleCN: 我们点了一份蒜香黄油龙虾。
senses.why: Because it is cooked and served as a dish, the animal name slides into the food it provides.
senses.whyCN: 因为它被烹饪后装盘上桌，动物的名字就自然而然转指它提供的食物。

senses.title: The colour of a cooked shell
senses.definition: a bright orange-red colour like the shell of a cooked lobster
senses.definitionCN: 像煮熟龙虾壳那样的明亮橘红色
senses.example: She wore a lobster swimsuit on the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿着龙虾色泳装在海滩上。
senses.why: Cooking turns the dark shell bright red, so the colour often shows up as a shade word and a sunburn joke in British English.
senses.whyCN: 烹煮让深色外壳变得鲜红，因此这个词在英国英语中常作颜色词，也用来开玩笑说人被晒得通红。

senses.title: The catch and the trade
senses.definition: lobsters as a catch or as an industry
senses.definitionCN: 作为渔获的龙虾或围绕它的产业
senses.example: The season brought the best lobster in years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个季节捕到了多年来最好的龙虾。
senses.why: A countable animal becomes an uncountable trade good when it is discussed in bulk.
senses.whyCN: 可数的动物在批量论及时就变成了不可数的商品，于是产生「渔获、产业」这一层用法。

senses.title: A Christmas staple
senses.definition: a fancy dish associated with special occasions in some cultures
senses.definitionCN: 在某些文化中被视作节庆场合的高级菜
senses.example: In some fishing villages, lobster is the Christmas dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 在一些渔村，龙虾是圣诞大餐的主角。
senses.why: In Atlantic fishing towns, lobster once ranked as cheap bait and only later became a festive luxury, a cultural reversal worth remembering.
senses.whyCN: 在大西洋沿岸渔村，龙虾一度是不值钱的诱饵，后来才变成节庆奢侈菜，这种文化上的翻转值得一提。

senses.title: Nicknames and slang
senses.definition: informal names, including old slang for a particular soldier uniform and modern nicknames
senses.definitionCN: 非正式称呼，包括旧时对某种军服的俚语以及现代绰号
senses.example: The old nickname lobster faded after the uniform changed.
senses.exampleCN: 军服换掉后，那个古老的绰号「龙虾」就不再流行。
senses.why: The bright red coat of some old British regiments looked like a cooked shell, so the animal name became a taunt.
senses.whyCN: 英国某些老式军团的鲜红军服看起来像煮熟的虾壳，于是这个动物名被用来起外号。

intro.en: Lobster comes from Old English loppestre, combining loppe, a spider, with the word for a plaited basket, with influence from Latin locusta.
intro.cn: lobster 来自古英语 loppestre，由 loppe（蜘蛛）与「编织篮子」一词组合而成，并受拉丁语 locusta 影响。

items.en: Loppestre names the creature, built on loppe meaning a spider.
items.cn: 古英语 loppestre 用来指这种动物，构词基础是意为「蜘蛛」的 loppe。

items.en: Latin locusta, a locust or a sea crustacean, may have shaped the ending.
items.cn: 拉丁语 locusta（蝗虫或海生甲壳类）可能影响了词尾的形式。

items.en: Old French lopeste and its later forms spread the word along the coast.
items.cn: 古法语 lopeste 及其后来的形式让这个词沿着海岸线传播开来。

items.en: Spellings such as lopster and lobster compete before one wins.
items.cn: lopster、lobster 等拼写各行其道，最终 lobster 胜出。

items.en: The word extends to the meat, then to a colour and to nicknames.
items.cn: 这个词从动物扩展到龙虾肉，再扩展到颜色和绰号。

note.en: Lobster belongs to a small shelled-seafood family with crayfish, crab, and shrimp, and its ending invites confusion with spinster and gangster.
note.cn: lobster 属于小龙虾、螃蟹、虾这一类带壳海鲜的词族，它那个 -ster 词尾又容易和 spinster、gangster 混起来。

entries.definition: an old word describing armour made of overlapping plates
entries.definitionCN: 古旧形容词：形容像龙虾壳那样以片状甲片连接的盔甲，由 lobster 加 -ed 构成

entries.definition: an old-fashioned word for a woman who has never married
entries.definitionCN: 旧称未婚女子的词，与 lobster 共享 -ster 词尾，但词根完全不同

entries.definition: a member of a criminal gang
entries.definitionCN: 黑帮成员，同样带 -ster 词尾，词根与龙虾无关

entries.definition: a small freshwater animal like a lobster
entries.definitionCN: 像龙虾的小型淡水晶虾

entries.definition: a sea animal with a wide shell and sideways walk
entries.definitionCN: 横行、壳宽扁的螃蟹

entries.definition: a small sea creature with a long tail, used as food
entries.definitionCN: 长尾的小型虾类，可食用

normalIntro.en: Lobster wears two old pieces: loppe, a spider, plus a basket word, so it means a spider in a woven cage.
normalIntro.cn: lobster 由两块老料拼成：loppe（蜘蛛）加上一个「篮子」词，意思是编织笼子里的蜘蛛。

normal.en: A lobster pot is the woven trap, a natural partner for this basket-word.
normal.cn: lobster pot 就是编织的捕捞笼，正好呼应这个词里「篮子」的来源。

normal.en: Lobster tail and lobster bisque name the two most common dishes.
normal.cn: lobster tail 与 lobster bisque 是两道最常见的龙虾菜名。

normal.en: Related seafood words are crab, shrimp, and crayfish.
normal.cn: 相关海鲜词有 crab（螃蟹）、shrimp（虾）和 crayfish（小龙虾）。

normal.en: The -ster ending also appears in spinster and gangster, but those roots are unrelated.
normal.cn: -ster 词尾也见于 spinster 与 gangster，但这些词的词根与龙虾无关。

normal.en: Say the plural aloud: one lobster, two lobsters.
normal.cn: 把复数念出声：一只是 lobster，两只是 lobsters。

abstract.en: Picture a dark shell waving two big claws under a rock.
abstract.cn: 想象一只深色外壳的大家伙在礁石下挥着两只大钳子。

abstract.en: See a white plate holding a bright red tail in butter.
abstract.cn: 想象白盘子里卧着一条金黄油亮的红色虾尾。

abstract.en: Recall a sunburned holidaymaker the colour of a cooked shell.
abstract.cn: 回忆一个被晒得像熟虾壳一样红的度假客。

examples.en: Lobsters hide in rock crevices during the day.
examples.cn: 龙虾白天躲在礁石缝里。

examples.en: The local market sells fresh lobster every morning.
examples.cn: 当地市场每天早上出售新鲜龙虾。

examples.en: He turned lobster red after an hour in the sun.
examples.cn: 他在太阳下待了一小时，晒得像熟龙虾一样红。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「老不死」——传说龙虾活得很久，老也死不了；这只是谐音玩笑，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 loppestre（loppe 蜘蛛 + 篮子类词）→ 中古英语 lopster/lobster → 现代英语 lobster，核心是「编织笼里挥大钳的甲壳动物」。

sensesIntro.en: Lobster begins as an animal name, then moves to its meat, its colour, its trade, its festive role, and finally to nicknames.
sensesIntro.cn: lobster 先是一个动物名，再延伸指肉、颜色、渔获生意、节庆角色，最后落到绰号与俚语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red shelled climber waving two big claws among rocks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只红壳家伙在礁石间挥着两只大钳子爬行。

branches.en: The living animal is the base sense.
branches.cn: 活着的动物是基础义项。

branches.en: From animal to food and to a whole harvest.
branches.cn: 从动物转到食物，再转到整季渔获。

branches.en: The cooked shell gives the colour sense.
branches.cn: 熟壳的鲜红引出颜色义。

branches.en: The dish and the festival reinforce each other.
branches.cn: 这道菜与节庆文化彼此强化。

branches.en: The red coat created the old soldier nickname.
branches.cn: 红色军服催生了旧日的士兵绰号。

intro.en: Lobster carries an old -ster ending and builds compounds such as lobsterman and lobstering.
intro.cn: lobster 带着古老的 -ster 词尾，并构成 lobsterman、lobstering 等复合词与派生词。

latinIntro.en: The ending may owe something to Latin locusta, which named locusts and some sea crustaceans.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的词尾可能受拉丁语 locusta 影响，后者既指蝗虫，也指某些海生甲壳类。

items.example: Loppe supplies the first part of the word.
items.exampleCN: loppe 提供了这个词的前一部分。

items.meaningCN: 有钳的大型海生甲壳动物
items.example: Lobster is the modern form.
items.exampleCN: lobster 是现代的拼写形式。

items.example: The plural simply adds s.
items.exampleCN: 复数直接加 s。

items.meaningCN: 表示人或从事者的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ster appears in lobster and spinster.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ster 出现在 lobster 与 spinster 中。

items.example: Lobsterman joins lobster and man.
items.exampleCN: lobsterman 由 lobster 与 man 拼合而成。

items.example: Lobstering is common along the coast.
items.exampleCN: 沿海一带捕龙虾很常见。

items.example: The suffix -ish forms lobsterish.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ish 构成 lobsterish。

items.example: Lobsterish is playful and rare.
items.exampleCN: lobsterish 是玩笑式的罕见用法。

items.example: A lobster pot echoes the old basket sense.
items.exampleCN: lobster pot 呼应了词源中的「篮子」义。

latinEntries.meaning: a locust, also a sea crustacean

definition_zh: 地点；地区；区域；所在地；位置
definition_en: a particular area or place, especially a small one or a neighbourhood
core_image: 地图上一个被铅笔圈出来的小街区，圈里只标了一处地名
scene: 地图上被红笔圈出的那片街区，是警方重点关注的地方。The police patrol the locality around the market every evening.
sceneCN: 这里 locality 是「地区、一带」（第 1 个义项：特定的地方或区域）；句意：警方每晚都在市场周边这一带巡逻。

pos.zh: 所在地；位置（生物学、统计中用法）

derivatives.zh: locus 加 -al 构成的形容词，义为「当地的；地方的」，也是 locality 的词根基础
由 local 加 -ize 构成，义为「使本地化；定位」
由 localize 加 -ation 构成，义为「本地化；定位」
由 locus 派生的动词，义为「确定位置；位于」

senses.title: A particular area
senses.definition: a particular area or neighbourhood, especially a small one
senses.definitionCN: 某个特定的地区或街区，通常指较小的范围
senses.example: Rainfall in this locality is unusually heavy.
senses.exampleCN: 这一带的降雨量异常大。
senses.why: The Latin root locus means a place, and the suffix -ity turns it into the quality or state of being a place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 locus 意为「地方」，后缀 -ity 把它变成「作为一个地方的状态」，因此指一片具体的地区。

senses.title: Where something sits
senses.definition: the place where a particular thing is located
senses.definitionCN: 某事物所处的地点或位置
senses.example: Scientists recorded the locality of every sample.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家记录了每一个样本的采集地点。
senses.why: If the word names the state of being in a place, it naturally comes to mean the spot a thing occupies.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词表示「处于某地」的状态，转而表示事物所占的那一处位置就顺理成章。

senses.title: Evacuate the locality
senses.titleCN: 撤离该地区（行政与防灾语境）
senses.definition: the area covered by an official notice or an emergency order
senses.definitionCN: 官方通告或紧急命令所覆盖的区域
senses.example: Officials told everyone to leave the locality at once.
senses.exampleCN: 官方要求所有人立即撤离该地区。
senses.why: Officials need a neutral word for the patch of land under an order, and a small area fits best.
senses.whyCN: 官方需要一个中性词来指命令覆盖的那片土地，而「一小片区域」的说法最为贴切。

senses.title: Local knowledge
senses.definition: the local conditions, customs, or features of a place
senses.definitionCN: 某地的当地条件、风俗或特点
senses.example: The guide knew the locality better than any map.
senses.exampleCN: 那位向导比任何地图都更了解当地情况。
senses.why: From the area itself the word extends to what people know about that area, its habits and character.
senses.whyCN: 从地方本身延伸出去，这个词也指人们对该地方的了解，即它的习性与特点。

senses.title: Type locality
senses.definition: the place where a species or rock type was first found and named
senses.definitionCN: 某一物种或岩石类型首次被发现并被命名的地方
senses.example: The type locality of the fossil lies in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 这种化石的模式产地就在这片丘陵中。
senses.why: Taxonomy needs a fixed anchor place for each name, so locality becomes a technical label.
senses.whyCN: 分类学需要为每个名称固定一个锚定地点，于是 locality 成为专业术语。

senses.title: Recall to the locality
senses.definition: a legal term limiting someone to a certain district
senses.definitionCN: 法律用语，指把某人限制在某个地区内
senses.example: The court ordered him to stay within the locality.
senses.exampleCN: 法院命令他留在这个地区内。
senses.why: Old law borrowed the word for the district a court could bind a person to stay inside.
senses.whyCN: 旧时法律借用这个词，指法院可以把人限制在其中不得离开的那一地区。

intro.en: Locality is built on Latin locus, a place, plus the noun suffix -ity, with the form passing through French.
intro.cn: locality 由拉丁语 locus（地方）加名词后缀 -ity 构成，其形式经由法语进入英语。

items.en: Locus means a place or a spot.
items.cn: 拉丁语 locus 意为地方、地点。

items.en: Localis means belonging to a place.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 localis 意为属于某地的。

items.en: Localite carries the abstract noun into French.
items.cn: 古法语 localite 把这个抽象名词带入法语。

items.en: Locality enters English as a learned word for a place.
items.cn: locality 在十六世纪作为书面学术词进入英语，指一个地方。

items.en: The word grows scientific uses such as type locality and legal uses.
items.cn: 现代英语中它发展出模式产地等科学用法以及法律用法。

note.en: Locality is the abstract noun of place, close to its own root local and to area, district, and neighbourhood.
note.cn: locality 是表示「地方」的抽象名词，与它的词根 local 以及 area、district、neighbourhood 语义相邻。

entries.definition: relating to a particular area
entries.definitionCN: 当地的；地方性的（locality 的词根形容词）

entries.definition: the plural of locality, naming several areas
entries.definitionCN: localities 是 locality 的复数形式，指多个地区

entries.definition: to find or fix the position of something
entries.definitionCN: 确定位置；定位（同出 locus 词根）

entries.definition: a part of a place or space
entries.definitionCN: 地区；区域（最通用的说法）

entries.definition: an official part of a town or country
entries.definitionCN: 行政区；城区

entries.definition: the area around where people live
entries.definitionCN: 街区；邻里一带

normalIntro.en: Locality is locus plus -ity, so it is the quality of being a place, that is, an area.
normalIntro.cn: locality 就是 locus 加 -ity，即「作为一个地方的状态」，也就是一片区域。

normal.en: The root local comes from locus, a place; locality is its abstract noun.
normal.cn: 词根 local 来自 locus（地方），locality 则是它的抽象名词。

normal.en: Locate, local, and locality all share the same place root.
normal.cn: locate、local、locality 共享同一个「地方」词根。

normal.en: In the locality replaces in the area in more formal texts.
normal.cn: 在正式文本里，in the locality 常用来代替 in the area。

normal.en: Type locality is the fixed home place of a species name.
normal.cn: type locality 是一个物种名称的固定「老家」。

normal.en: Plural is localities, swapping y for ies.
normal.cn: 复数是 localities，把 y 换成 ies。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil ring around one block on a map.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上一个街区被铅笔圈起来。

abstract.en: See a small red pin marking exactly where a specimen was found.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚小红针精确标出标本被发现的位置。

abstract.en: Imagine a loudspeaker telling a whole district to leave.
abstract.cn: 想象一个喇叭对着整片区域喊大家撤离。

examples.en: Few shops in the locality open after dark.
examples.cn: 这一带没有几家店在天黑后营业。

examples.en: The plant grows only in a few localities along the coast.
examples.cn: 这种植物只生长在沿岸少数几个地方。

examples.en: Historians studied the locality of the old mine.
examples.cn: 历史学家考察了那座老矿的位置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「楼开了一体」——楼开了合成一体，围出一片区域；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 locus（地方）→ 晚期拉丁语 localis（属于某地的）→ 古法语 localite → 英语 locality，核心义「被圈定的一片地方」。

sensesIntro.en: Locality starts as a particular area, then names where something sits, spreads to official and legal districts, and picks up scientific and local-knowledge uses.
sensesIntro.cn: locality 先指特定的地区，再指某物所在的位置，扩展到官方与法律的辖区，并获得科学术语和地方知识两类用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pencil ring drawn around one small block on a map.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上用一个铅笔圈围出一小片街区。

branches.en: A particular area is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 特定的地区是日常义项。

branches.en: Where a thing sits is the location sense.
branches.cn: 物品所在之处是位置义项。

branches.en: Official notices and old law both bind people to a district.
branches.cn: 官方通告与旧时法律都把人限制在某个辖区内。

branches.en: Knowing the area is knowing the locality.
branches.cn: 了解一片区域就是了解当地情况。

branches.en: The type locality fixes a named place for science.
branches.cn: 模式产地为科学命名固定了一处地点。

intro.en: Locality is locus plus the abstract noun suffix -ity, and it opens a large family: local, locate, location, and localize.
intro.cn: locality 是 locus 加抽象名词后缀 -ity，并牵出 local、locate、location、localize 这一大家族。

latinIntro.en: Latin locus means a place; localis, belonging to a place, and locare, to place, come from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 locus 意为地方，localis（属于某地的）与 locare（放置）都由此而来。

items.example: Locus is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: locus 是整个词族的词根。

items.meaningCN: 学术用语中借用为「位点」
items.example: The locus of the mutation lies on one gene.
items.exampleCN: 这个突变的位点位于某一个基因上。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity turns local into locality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 把 local 变成 locality。

items.example: Locality names the area itself.
items.exampleCN: locality 指区域本身。

items.example: Local means belonging to a nearby place.
items.exampleCN: local 表示属于附近某地。

items.example: Location is the place a thing occupies.
items.exampleCN: location 指事物占据的地点。

items.example: To locate is to find where something is.
items.exampleCN: locate 就是找出某物在哪里。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms localize.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ize 构成 localize。

items.meaning: to make local or to fix a place
items.example: Localize keeps the meaning of place.
items.exampleCN: localize 保留了地方的语义。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms localization.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 localization。

definition_zh: 储物柜；锁柜；冷藏柜
definition_en: a small cupboard or cabinet with a lock, used for storing personal things
core_image: 一排带锁的小柜门，每扇后面放着一只运动包
scene: 体育馆更衣室里，队员们换好球衣，把手机和钱包塞进带锁的柜子。Players leave their phones in a locker before training.
sceneCN: 这里 locker 是「储物柜」（第 1 个义项：可上锁存放私人物品的柜子）；句意：队员们在训练前把手机放进储物柜。

derivatives.zh: 上锁；是 locker 的基础词，指用钥匙或密码关住
锁着的；由 lock 加 -ed 构成，描述被关住的状态
可上锁的；lock 加 -able，强调能装锁

senses.title: A small cupboard kept under lock
senses.definition: a small cupboard or cabinet with a lock, used by one person at school, work, or a sports centre
senses.definitionCN: 学校、单位或运动场馆里供个人使用的带锁小柜子
senses.example: She pinned the timetable inside her locker door.
senses.exampleCN: 她把课表贴在自己储物柜门的内侧。
senses.why: A locker is simply a thing that locks, so the word starts with a small store that can be shut tight.
senses.whyCN: locker 本质是「能锁住的东西」，所以最基础的义项就是一间可以关严的小储藏空间。

senses.title: A closed drawer in a public place
senses.definition: one of a set of locked drawers or boxes in a bank, gym, or station for keeping valuables
senses.definitionCN: 银行、健身房或车站里供存放贵重物品的一组上锁抽屉或格子
senses.example: Travellers pay by the hour to use the terminal lockers.
senses.exampleCN: 旅客按小时付费使用车站的寄存柜。
senses.why: The same locked box is repeated in rows, and each one is rented for a short time.
senses.whyCN: 同一种带锁的箱子成排摆放、按时间出租，于是义项扩展到公共场所的自助寄存柜。

senses.title: A chilled storage box
senses.definition: a large chilled cabinet on a ship or in a restaurant for keeping food cold
senses.definitionCN: 船上或餐馆里用于低温保存食物的大型冷藏储物柜
senses.example: The catch was stored in the ship frozen locker.
senses.exampleCN: 渔获被存放在船上的冷冻柜里。
senses.why: At sea a chilled compartment that can be locked became a locker for food, the same box with a cold purpose.
senses.whyCN: 船上能上锁的隔间被用来冷藏食物，于是同一个带锁的箱子加上了低温用途。

intro.en: Locker is formed in English from lock plus -er, an agent suffix meaning the thing that does or holds.
intro.cn: locker 是在英语内部由 lock 加词尾 -er 构成的，-er 表示「做事或装东西的物件」。

items.en: Loc means a fastening or a bolt, the earliest English form of lock.
items.cn: 古英语 loc 指门闩或扣件，是现代 lock 的最早形式。

items.en: A lock is a device that holds a door shut and needs a key to open.
items.cn: lock 指能关紧门、需要钥匙才能打开的装置。

items.en: The suffix -er is added to name the thing that locks, first a fastener and later a box.
items.cn: 加上词尾 -er 用来命名「能锁住的物件」，先指扣件，后指箱柜。

items.en: In the 19th century locker settles as a small private cupboard for school or sport.
items.cn: 进入十九世纪，locker 固定指学校或运动场里的私人小柜。

items.en: Twentieth-century usage extends it to public rental boxes and chilled compartments.
items.cn: 二十世纪的用法再扩展到公共寄存格与冷藏隔间。

note.en: Locker is a locking storage box; its family is lock, locked, and lockable, while nearby words name other kinds of furniture.
note.cn: locker 是能上锁的储物箱；它的同族词有 lock、locked、lockable，而邻近的词则指其他类型的家具。

entries.definition: to shut something with a key or code
entries.definitionCN: 用钥匙或密码锁上；locker 的基础词

entries.definition: shut and fastened with a lock
entries.definitionCN: 锁着的；由 lock 加 -ed 构成

entries.definition: a small pendant that opens to hold a photo
entries.definitionCN: 可翻开装照片的小吊坠盒；与 locker 同用 lock 词干，只是小得多

entries.definition: a piece of furniture with doors for storing things
entries.definitionCN: 带门的橱柜；一般不强调上锁

entries.definition: a cupboard with shelves or drawers, often for valuables
entries.definitionCN: 带隔板或抽屉的柜子，常用来放贵重物品

entries.definition: one section of a larger space set apart for storage
entries.definitionCN: 从大空间中隔出来的一块储物区域

normalIntro.en: Locker is lock plus -er: the box whose defining job is to stay shut.
normalIntro.cn: locker 是 lock 加 -er：它的本职就是把东西锁住。

normal.en: Lock plus -er gives locker, the thing that locks.
normal.cn: lock 加 -er 得到 locker，即「能锁住的东西」。

normal.en: At school you pin notes inside your locker.
normal.cn: 在学校里，你把便条贴在储物柜里侧。

normal.en: A locker room is where players change and store kit.
normal.cn: locker room 是球员换装、放装备的更衣室。

normal.en: Airports and stations rent lockers by the hour.
normal.cn: 机场和车站按小时出租寄存柜。

normal.en: Compare cupboard: a cupboard may stay unlocked, a locker is built to lock.
normal.cn: 对比 cupboard：橱柜可以不上锁，locker 天生就是用来上锁的。

abstract.en: Picture a row of small doors, each with a padlock, each holding a pair of sports shoes.
abstract.cn: 想象一排小柜门，每扇都挂着锁，每扇后面放着一双运动鞋。

abstract.en: Think of the clicking sound of a metal coin being pushed into a rental box.
abstract.cn: 想想硬币被按进自助寄存柜时那一声轻响。

abstract.en: Imagine freezing air escaping when a ship storage door is opened.
abstract.cn: 想象打开船舱储物间时，一股冷气涌出来。

examples.en: Please put your bag in the locker and take the key.
examples.cn: 请把包放进储物柜，然后拿走钥匙。

examples.en: The school bought new lockers for the first-year students.
examples.cn: 学校为一年级学生买了新的储物柜。

examples.en: He forgot the code to his locker in the gym.
examples.cn: 他忘了健身房里自己储物柜的密码。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「洛克」——一位叫洛克的同学总把自己的东西锁进柜子，locker 就是那排锁柜；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 loc（门闩、扣件）→ lock（锁）＋ 词尾 -er → locker（能锁住的物件）→ 演变为 14 世纪后的扣件、19 世纪后的小柜，核心义「能关严锁住的箱柜」。

sensesIntro.en: Locker starts as a box that locks, spreads to rented drawers in public places, and ends as a chilled storeroom crate on ships.
sensesIntro.cn: locker 从能上锁的箱子出发，扩展到公共场所的自助寄存格，最后指向船上的冷藏储物间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of small locked doors, each hiding a personal bag.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排带锁的小柜门，每扇后面都藏着私人物品。

branches.en: The private school or gym cupboard is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 学校或健身房里的私人柜子是日常义项。

branches.en: Public rental boxes apply the same lock to shared space.
branches.cn: 公共寄存柜把同一把锁用到共享空间里。

branches.en: The chilled sea store is the specialised sense.
branches.cn: 船上的冷藏储物间是专业义项。

branches.en: Both are boxes rented or assigned for a short and private use.
branches.cn: 两者都是短期、私密使用的储物箱。

branches.en: A chilled locker is still first a locked compartment.
branches.cn: 冷藏柜首先仍是一个能锁上的隔间。

intro.en: Locker is a native English compound of lock and the thing suffix -er.
intro.cn: locker 是英语本土构词：lock 加表示「物件」的词尾 -er。

latinIntro.en: Locker has no Latin source; lock and the suffix -er both come from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: locker 没有拉丁语来源；lock 与词尾 -er 都来自古英语。

items.example: The old word lock named the bar on a door.
items.exampleCN: 古老的 lock 指门上的横闩。

items.meaning: a thing that does or holds
items.meaningCN: 表示从事或承载动作之物的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er turns lock into locker.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 把 lock 变成 locker。

items.example: Locker keeps the whole family together.
items.exampleCN: locker 把整个词族收在一起。

items.example: The door stayed locked all night.
items.exampleCN: 那扇门整夜都锁着。

items.example: The suffix -able forms lockable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 lockable。

items.example: Every desk drawer was lockable.
items.exampleCN: 每个抽屉都能上锁。

items.example: The suffix -et forms locket.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -et 构成 locket。

items.example: A locket holds a photo close to the heart.
items.exampleCN: 吊坠盒把照片贴近心口。

items.example: Locker room is a fixed compound.
items.exampleCN: locker room 是固定搭配。

definition_zh: 高耸的；崇高的；高傲的
definition_en: very high and impressive, or noble in aim, or showing proud superiority
core_image: 山巅上一座极高的塔，塔中人抬手示意旁人退开
scene: 山脉尽头，一座教堂尖顶刺入云层，游客抬头仰望。A lofty tower rises far above the valley.
sceneCN: 这里 lofty 是「高耸的」（第 1 个义项：高度惊人、令人仰望）；句意：一座高耸的塔远远高出山谷。

derivatives.zh: 高傲地；高高地；由 lofty 加 -ly 构成
高耸；崇高；高傲；由 lofty 加 -ness 构成
阁楼；lofty 的基础：指楼顶下方的上层空间

senses.title: Rising very high
senses.definition: very high and tall, so that people look up at it
senses.definitionCN: 非常高，高到需要仰头观看
senses.example: Tall poplars line the road to the lofty peak.
senses.exampleCN: 高大的杨树沿着通往高耸山峰的路排列。
senses.why: The word is built on loft, the upper floor of a building, so the basic sense is simply the quality of being high up.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建在 loft（楼的上层）之上，所以最基本的义项就是「位置高的性质」。

senses.title: Noble in aim
senses.definition: of an idea or purpose so good and ambitious that it lifts people above ordinary concerns
senses.definitionCN: 思想或目标美好而远大，把人提升到日常琐事之上
senses.example: The charity was founded on lofty ideals of fairness.
senses.exampleCN: 这个慈善机构建立在公平的崇高理想之上。
senses.why: Something physically high is admired, so a high aim becomes a noble aim.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的高处令人敬仰，于是高远的目标被引申为崇高的目标。

senses.title: Proudly above others
senses.definition: behaving as if you are more important than other people
senses.definitionCN: 表现得仿佛自己比别人更重要的样子
senses.example: His lofty manner made the new staff uneasy.
senses.exampleCN: 他那种高傲的做派让新员工感到不安。
senses.why: Someone standing too high looks down on those below, so height turns into haughty distance.
senses.whyCN: 站得太高的人自然俯视下方，于是「高」变成了居高临下的疏离。

intro.en: Lofty is formed in English from loft, the upper floor of a house, plus the suffix -y.
intro.cn: lofty 是在英语内部由 loft（房子的上层）加词尾 -y 构成的。

items.en: Loft means the air, the sky, or an upper room.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 loft 指空气、天空，或楼上的房间。

items.en: Loft enters English meaning the upper part of a house, later a roof space.
items.cn: loft 进入英语，指房屋的上层，后来指屋顶下的空间。

items.en: The suffix -y adds a quality, so lofty first means high or airy.
items.cn: 词尾 -y 表示性质，lofty 最初指「高的、空中的」。

items.en: The word is borrowed for noble aims and for proud, haughty behaviour.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，这个词被借用来形容崇高的目标与高傲的举止。

items.en: Modern English keeps all three threads: height, nobility, and haughtiness.
items.cn: 现代英语保留三条脉络：高度、崇高与高傲。

note.en: Lofty is the adjective of loft; its family is loftily and loftiness, and its near words are other height adjectives.
note.cn: lofty 是 loft 的形容词形式；同族词有 loftily、loftiness，近义词是其他表示高的形容词。

entries.definition: the space under the roof of a building
entries.definitionCN: 屋顶下的空间；阁楼，是 lofty 的基础词

entries.definition: in a proud or high manner
entries.definitionCN: 高傲地；高高地；由 lofty 加 -ly 构成

entries.definition: the quality of being high, noble, or proud
entries.definitionCN: 高耸、崇高或高傲的性质；由 lofty 加 -ness 构成

entries.definition: extremely tall and impressive
entries.definitionCN: 极高耸、令人震撼的；只强调高度

entries.definition: of the highest beauty or moral worth
entries.definitionCN: 极美的；崇高的；语气比 lofty 更重

entries.definition: showing cold pride and contempt for others
entries.definitionCN: 傲慢冷淡、看不起别人；缺乏 lofty 的「崇高」含义

entries.definition: measuring a great distance from bottom to top
entries.definitionCN: 高的；最普通的说法，没有 lofty 的文学和比喻色彩

normalIntro.en: Lofty is loft plus -y: something with the quality of an upper floor, so up high and far above.
normalIntro.cn: lofty 是 loft 加 -y：具有「楼上」的性质，所以高远在众人之上。

normal.en: Loft plus -y builds lofty from the word for an upper floor.
normal.cn: loft 加 -y 构成 lofty，基础词是「楼上的空间」。

normal.en: A house can be converted into a loft apartment.
normal.cn: 房子可以改造成阁楼公寓。

normal.en: Lofty ambitions mean aims set very high.
normal.cn: lofty ambitions 指定得很高的志向。

normal.en: A lofty tone suggests someone looking down on others.
normal.cn: lofty tone 暗示有人俯视别人。

normal.en: Compare high: high is neutral, lofty is literary and carries admiration or disdain.
normal.cn: 对比 high：high 中立，lofty 偏文学，带有敬仰或轻蔑的味道。

abstract.en: Picture a tower whose top disappears into the clouds.
abstract.cn: 想象一座塔，塔顶没入云中。

abstract.en: Think of a ladder climbing towards something only a dream can reach.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子伸向只有梦想才够得着的地方。

abstract.en: Imagine someone speaking from a high balcony, never coming down to the crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象有人站在高台上说话，从不下来走到人群中。

examples.en: Lofty cliffs guard the northern coast of the island.
examples.cn: 高耸的峭壁守护着岛屿的北岸。

examples.en: The project began with lofty goals but little funding.
examples.cn: 这个项目起步时目标宏大，资金却很少。

examples.en: She disliked his lofty attitude towards junior staff.
examples.cn: 她讨厌他对下级员工的傲慢态度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「楼梯」——阁楼的楼梯一层层往上，站得越高越显得 lofty 高耸，甚至高傲；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古诺斯语 loft（空气、上层）→ 古英语 loft（房屋上层；阁楼）＋ 词尾 -y → lofty，核心义「高高在上」。

sensesIntro.en: Lofty keeps its three threads: the height itself, the nobility of a high aim, and the pride of someone too far above.
sensesIntro.cn: lofty 保留三条脉络：高度本身、高远目标带来的崇高，以及高高在上者的傲慢。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tower at the top of a mountain, with people below looking up.
core.cn: 核心意象：山顶的塔，众人从下方仰望。

branches.en: The physical height sense is the basic one.
branches.cn: 物理高度是最基本的义项。

branches.en: A high aim becomes a noble aim in the moral sense.
branches.cn: 高远的目标在道德层面变成崇高的目标。

branches.en: Standing above others becomes a proud attitude.
branches.cn: 站在他人之上变成了傲慢的态度。

branches.en: Both share the image of lifting something up.
branches.cn: 两者共享「被抬高」的意象。

branches.en: Highness can be admired as nobility or mocked as pride.
branches.cn: 「高」既可以被赞为崇高，也可以被讥为傲慢。

intro.en: Lofty is a native English adjective made from loft and the quality suffix -y.
intro.cn: lofty 是英语本土形容词，由 loft 加表性质的词尾 -y 构成。

latinIntro.en: Lofty has no Latin source; loft comes from Old Norse, and the suffix -y is native to English.
latinIntro.cn: lofty 没有拉丁语来源；loft 来自古诺斯语，词尾 -y 是英语本土成分。

items.example: Old Norse loft gave English the upper floor.
items.exampleCN: 古诺斯语 loft 给英语带来了「上层」之意。

items.example: The suffix -y turns loft into lofty.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 把 loft 变成 lofty。

items.example: Lofty keeps all three meanings alive.
items.exampleCN: lofty 三种含义都保留着。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms loftily.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 loftily。

items.example: She loftily dismissed every objection.
items.exampleCN: 她高傲地否定了每一个反对意见。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms loftiness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 loftiness。

items.meaning: the state of being high or proud
items.example: The loftiness of the hall surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 大厅的高敞令我们惊讶。

items.example: The suffix -er forms loftier.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 loftier。

items.example: The suffix -est forms loftiest.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -est 构成 loftiest。

definition_zh: 逻辑上；合乎逻辑地；按理说
definition_en: in a way that follows clear reasoning, or as the evidence suggests it should be
core_image: 一条条链环从前提连到结论，每一环都扣得严丝合缝
scene: 审稿人逐句检查论证，发现每一步推导都接得上，结论自然推出。The argument is constructed logically from start to finish.
sceneCN: 这里 logically 是「合乎逻辑地」（第 1 个义项：按清晰推理的步骤进行）；句意：这个论证自始至终都合乎逻辑地构建起来。

derivatives.zh: 逻辑；论理；logically 的基础名词，源自希腊语 logos
合乎逻辑的；有道理的；由 logic 加 -al 构成
不合逻辑的；由否定前缀 il- 加 logical 构成

senses.title: By clear reasoning
senses.titleCN: 合乎逻辑地；逻辑严密地
senses.definition: in a way that follows step by step from clear reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 按照清晰推理一步一步推进的方式
senses.example: She usually argues logically, even under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 她即使在压力之下，通常也能合乎逻辑地论证。
senses.why: The word is built on logic, from Greek logos meaning reason, so logically means according to a chain of reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建在 logic 之上，而 logic 源自希腊语 logos（理性），所以 logically 就是「依照推理链进行」。

senses.title: Of necessity, by inference
senses.definition: in a way that necessarily follows from the stated facts
senses.definitionCN: 以从既定事实必然推出的方式
senses.example: Logically, if all costs rise, prices must follow.
senses.exampleCN: 从逻辑上说，如果所有成本都上涨，价格必然随之上调。
senses.why: When one step forces the next, the adverb marks a conclusion forced by inference.
senses.whyCN: 当一步必然导出下一步时，这个副词就标记出由推理得出的结论。

senses.title: As one would expect
senses.definition: in the way that sensible expectation suggests, in ordinary speech
senses.definitionCN: 在日常口语中表示「按常理应当如此」
senses.example: Logically, the bus should have arrived by now.
senses.exampleCN: 按理说，公交车现在该到了。
senses.why: Everyday guessing borrows the authority of strict inference, so logically can simply mean as expected.
senses.whyCN: 日常判断借助严密推理的权威语气，于是 logically 也可以只表示「按预期」。

intro.en: Logically is the adverb of logic, built from Greek logos plus English suffixes -ic and -al.
intro.cn: logically 是 logic 的副词形式，由希腊语 logos 加英语词尾 -ic、-al 与 -ly 构成。

items.en: Logos means a word, an account, or reason itself.
items.cn: 希腊语 logos 指词语、叙述，也指理性本身。

items.en: Logike in Aristotle names the science of correct reasoning.
items.cn: 亚里士多德使用的 logike 指关于正确推理的学问。

items.en: Latin logica carries the name of the discipline into the schools.
items.cn: 拉丁语 logica 把这门学科的名称带进中世纪的学校。

items.en: Logique enters English as the name of the discipline of reasoned argument.
items.cn: logique 进入英语，成为推理学科的名称。

items.en: Logically appears as the adverb meaning in accordance with reasoning.
items.cn: logically 作为副词出现，意为「依据推理地」。

items.en: Modern English adds the looser spoken sense of as expected.
items.cn: 现代英语又增添了口语中「按理说」的宽松义项。

note.en: Logically is the adverb of logic; its family is logical, illogical, and logic, while nearby words name reasoning without a strict chain.
note.cn: logically 是 logic 的副词；同族有 logical、illogical、logic，近义词则指不依赖严格推链的说理方式。

entries.definition: the study or the use of correct reasoning
entries.definitionCN: 研究或运用正确推理的学问；是 logically 的基础名词

entries.definition: following clear reasoning
entries.definitionCN: 合乎逻辑的；由 logic 加 -al 构成

entries.definition: not following clear reasoning
entries.definitionCN: 不合逻辑的；否定前缀 il- 加 logical

entries.definition: in a way based on reason rather than feeling
entries.definitionCN: 理性地；强调不感情用事，而不强调推链

entries.definition: in the same way each time
entries.definitionCN: 一贯地；强调前后一致，不一定合乎逻辑

entries.definition: in a fair and sensible way
entries.definitionCN: 合理地；偏重公平与通情达理

normalIntro.en: Logically is logic plus -al plus -ly: the reasoning noun turned into the manner of reasoning.
normalIntro.cn: logically 是 logic 加 -al 再加 -ly：把「逻辑」这个名词变成「按逻辑的方式」。

normal.en: Logic plus the suffixes -al and -ly gives logically.
normal.cn: logic 依次加 -al 与 -ly 得到 logically。

normal.en: Greek logos means reason, and logic keeps that meaning.
normal.cn: 希腊语 logos 意为理性，logic 保留了这层含义。

normal.en: A logically sound argument survives every objection.
normal.cn: 逻辑严密的论证经得起任何质疑。

normal.en: The adverb typically begins with a comma at the start of a sentence.
normal.cn: 这个副词放句首时，通常后面跟一个逗号。

normal.en: Compare illogical: the prefix il- reverses the meaning entirely.
normal.cn: 对比 illogical：前缀 il- 把意思完全颠倒。

abstract.en: Picture a chain of metal links from the first line to the last, none broken.
abstract.cn: 想象一条由金属链环组成的链子，从第一行连到最后一行，环环不脱。

abstract.en: Think of a set of train tracks that meet exactly at each joint.
abstract.cn: 想象中的铁轨，每个接头都严丝合缝地对上。

abstract.en: Imagine a clock that shows the right time because the gears all fit.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，齿轮全部咬合，所以走时准确。

examples.en: The report is written logically and is easy to follow.
examples.cn: 这份报告写得合乎逻辑，读起来很容易跟上。

examples.en: Logically, a cheaper plan should attract more users.
examples.cn: 按理说，更便宜的方案应当吸引更多用户。

examples.en: He reasoned logically from the evidence, not from feeling.
examples.cn: 他依据证据合乎逻辑地推理，而不是凭感觉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「逻辑里」——事情全在「逻辑里」绕，一环扣一环，就是 logically 合乎逻辑地；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 logos（言语、理性）→ 希腊语 logike（推理论）→ 拉丁语 logica → 英语 logic + 词尾 -al + -ly → logically，核心义「按推链走」。

sensesIntro.en: Logically first names the manner of strict reasoning, then a necessary conclusion, and finally an everyday phrase meaning as expected.
sensesIntro.cn: logically 先指严格推理的方式，再指必然推出的结论，最后在日常口语中表示「按理说」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain of links joining premises to a conclusion.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条链环把前提一节节连到结论。

branches.en: Reasoning well is the everyday adverbial sense.
branches.cn: 合乎逻辑地推理是日常副词义项。

branches.en: A forced inference marks the technical sense.
branches.cn: 必然推出的结论是技术义项。

branches.en: Everyday expectation is the relaxed spoken sense.
branches.cn: 日常预期是宽松的口语义项。

branches.en: Both depend on a valid chain from premises.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖从前提出发的有效推链。

branches.en: Expectation is a mild version of necessary inference.
branches.cn: 预期是必然推理的轻度版本。

intro.en: Logically stacks three elements of logic, the noun of reasoning, with -al and -ly laid on top.
intro.cn: logically 在 logic 这个「推理」名词之上，叠加 -al 与 -ly 两个词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin logica is a borrowing of Greek logike, and both pass through logic into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 logica 借自希腊语 logike，二者经由 logic 进入英语。

items.example: Logos is the ancient root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: logos 是整个词族的古老词根。

items.example: The ending -ic marks logic as the discipline.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 使 logic 成为学科名。

items.example: Logic is the base of the adverb.
items.exampleCN: logic 是这个副词的基础。

items.meaningCN: 表示「与……相关的」形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -al forms logical.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 logical。

items.example: A logical step never skips the middle.
items.exampleCN: 合乎逻辑的一步从不跳过中间环节。

items.meaningCN: 表示「以……方式」的副词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ly forms logically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 logically。

items.example: Many sciences share the logos stem in -logy.
items.exampleCN: 许多学科都用 logos 词干构成的 -logy。

items.example: Illogical steps break the chain.
items.exampleCN: 不合逻辑的步骤会打断链条。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms logicality.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 logicality。

items.example: Logicality is rare in rush decisions.
items.exampleCN: 仓促决策中很难体现逻辑性。

definition_zh: 长寿；寿命长；（事物的）持久性；耐久年限
definition_en: the fact or length of a long life, and by extension the lasting quality or duration of a thing
core_image: 一条很长的时间线：小人一路走到线的最远处，脚步依然稳健
scene: 生日蜡烛插满整个蛋糕，家人围坐，笑着说老人记性比谁都好。Researchers link the village remarkable longevity to fresh food, daily walking and strong family ties.
sceneCN: 这里 longevity 是「长寿」（第 1 个义项：活得很长、寿命长久）；句意为研究者把村里人的长寿归因于新鲜食物、日常步行和紧密的亲情。

pos.zh: 长寿；寿命长；持久性；耐久年限

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁形容词 longaevus 进入英语，义为「长寿的；长命的」
由同一拉丁词根加形容词后缀构成，义为「长久的；长寿的」，用法较古旧

senses.title: The fact of living a long life
senses.definition: the state or fact of living for a long time, especially far beyond what is average
senses.definitionCN: 活得长久的状态或事实，尤指远超一般人
senses.example: The region is famous for the longevity of its residents.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区以居民长寿而闻名。
senses.why: Latin longus means long and aevum means age or lifetime, so longevity is literally a long lifetime.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 longus 意为「长」，aevum 意为「年龄、一生」，所以 longevity 字面就是「长的一生」，长寿该义项由此而来。

senses.title: The length of a life
senses.definition: the number of years that a person, animal or plant actually lives
senses.definitionCN: 人或动植物实际活着的年数
senses.example: Scientists study factors that affect average longevity.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家研究影响平均寿命的因素。
senses.why: Once the long span is named, the span itself can be measured, so the word also means how long the life lasts.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「长的一生」被命名，这一段生命也就可以计量，于是这个词也指寿命本身有多长。

senses.title: Durability of an object or product
senses.definition: the length of time that a product, building or piece of equipment continues to work well
senses.definitionCN: 产品、建筑或设备持续良好运作的时间长度
senses.example: Proper maintenance extends the longevity of a bicycle.
senses.exampleCN: 妥善保养能延长自行车的使用寿命。
senses.why: The same long-serving image moves from a body to a machine: a tool that lasts a long time is said to have longevity.
senses.whyCN: 同一幅「长久陪伴」的画面从身体移到器物上：能长久使用的工具就被说成有 longevity，即耐用年限。

senses.title: Lasting success of an idea or work
senses.definition: the fact of lasting or remaining popular, important or influential for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 长期保持流行、重要或影响力的事实
senses.example: Critics praise the longevity of the novel among teenage readers.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称赞这部小说在青少年读者中的持久影响力。
senses.why: A book or a custom can outlive its own era; the long lifetime becomes a metaphor for cultural staying power.
senses.whyCN: 一本书或一种习俗能比自己所属的时代活得更久；于是「长命」被用来比喻文化上的持久力。

senses.title: Length of service or time in a role
senses.definition: the length of time that someone serves in a job, office or company
senses.definitionCN: 某人在某个职位、机构或公司任职的时间长度
senses.example: Her longevity in the post reassured the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她在这个职位上任职之久，让整个团队感到安心。
senses.why: In the workplace the measuring tape of a lifetime measures tenure instead, and a long stay is praised with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 在职场上，量一生的皮尺改去量任期，待得长久也会用同一个词来称赞。

intro.en: Longevity comes from Late Latin longaevitas, built on longus, long, and aevum, age or lifetime.
intro.cn: longevity 来自晚期拉丁语 longaevitas，由 longus（长）与 aevum（年龄、一生）构成。

items.en: Longus means long and aevum means a lifetime or an age.
items.cn: longus 意为「长」，aevum 意为「一生、年代」。

items.en: Longaevus, long-lived, is an adjective recorded in Late Latin prose.
items.cn: longaevus 意为「长寿的」，是晚期拉丁语散文中有记录的形容词。

items.en: The abstract noun longaevitas, long life, is formed on that adjective.
items.cn: 抽象名词 longaevitas（长寿）由该形容词构成。

items.en: A French form of the noun appears before the English one.
items.cn: 该名词的法语形式先于英语形式出现。

items.en: Longevity enters English in the 1600s with the older spelling longaevity, used in medical writing.
items.cn: longevity 在十七世纪进入英语，早期拼作 longaevity，多用于医学写作。

items.en: Modern usage extends the word from human lifespan to products, careers and works of art.
items.cn: 现代用法把该词从人的寿命扩展到产品、职业生涯与艺术作品。

note.en: The first group gathers the rare adjectival relatives and near spellings; the second gathers words about how long a life lasts.
note.cn: 第一组收稀有的同族形容词与形近拼写；第二组收关于寿命长短的近义词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning long-lived, formed directly from the Latin longaevus.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「长寿的」，直接由拉丁语 longaevus 变来。

entries.definition: Running lengthwise or relating to length in space; it only shares the long- look and comes from a different sense of length.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「纵向的、长度的」；只是拼写相近，来自另一个表示空间「长」的词根，词源不同。

entries.definition: Distance east or west of the meridian, which is about length on a map, not length of life.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「经度」，指地图上沿东西方向丈量的长度，与寿命无关，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The length of time a person or thing exists, stated as a plain measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「寿命」，平实陈述存在的时间长度，不带「活得很长」的评价。

entries.definition: The ability of an object to keep working or to resist wear without breaking.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「耐用性」，强调物件抗磨损、不易损坏的能力。

entries.definition: The state of lasting forever or staying unchanged, stronger and more absolute than longevity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「永久性」，指永远持续、保持不变，比 longevity 更绝对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin roots longus and aevum, the family adjective, and the phrases the noun really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 longus 与 aevum、同族形容词，以及这个词真正出现的搭配。

normal.en: Break it as long- plus -ev-: long life.
normal.cn: 拆作 long 加 -ev-：long 是「长」，-ev- 来自 aevum（一生），合起来就是「长的一生」。

normal.en: Aevum also gives eternal and medieval, so -ev- points to an age or a lifetime.
normal.cn: aevum 还给出 eternal 与 medieval，所以 -ev- 指向「时代、一生」。

normal.en: The Latin adjective longaevus survives as the rare English adjective longevous.
normal.cn: 拉丁语形容词 longaevus 在英语里留下了一个罕见的形容词 longevous（长寿的）。

normal.en: Longevity research asks why some people live past a hundred.
normal.cn: longevity research 研究的就是为什么有些人能活过百岁。

normal.en: Compare lifespan: lifespan is the plain measure, longevity is a long lifespan or the ability to last.
normal.cn: 对比 lifespan：lifespan 是中性的「寿命长度」，longevity 强调「长寿」或「持久」。

abstract.en: Picture a very long ruler laid against a person age, marked from birth to old age.
abstract.cn: 想象一把很长的尺子贴着一个人的年龄铺开，从出生一直量到老年。

abstract.en: Think of the same ruler being used to measure a life, not just to describe it.
abstract.cn: 再想这把尺子不只描述寿命，还被用来测量寿命的长短。

abstract.en: Move the ruler onto a bicycle frame or a song: whatever lasts a very long time borrows the long line.
abstract.cn: 把这把尺子挪到自行车车架或一首歌上：凡是能长久存在的东西，都借用了那条长线。

examples.en: Genetic studies may explain why longevity runs in some families.
examples.cn: 基因研究也许能解释为什么某些家族代代长寿。

examples.en: A mild climate and a simple diet are often linked to longevity.
examples.cn: 温和的气候与简单的饮食常被认为与长寿有关。

examples.en: Careful design greatly increases the longevity of street furniture.
examples.cn: 精心设计能大幅提高街道设施的耐用年限。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弄脚位」——脚走得越久，路就越长：长寿；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 longus「长」+ aevum「一生、年代」→ 晚期拉丁语形容词 longaevus「长寿的」→ 抽象名词 longaevitas「长寿」→ 经法语进入英语，早期拼作 longaevity，核心义「长的一生」，后引申为「持久」。

sensesIntro.en: Longevity first names a long human life, then the measured length of that life, and then the same lasting quality in products, works, ideas and careers.
sensesIntro.cn: longevity 先指人的长寿，再指寿命的长短，随后把这种「活得久」的品质移到产品、作品、观念与任职年限上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a very long timeline along which a small figure keeps walking to the far end.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条很长的时间线，小人一路走到线的最远处，脚步依然稳健。

branches.en: THE BODY: a long human life is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 身体线：人的长寿是字面义项。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: the same long life becomes a number of years.
branches.cn: 计量线：同一段长寿变成了具体的年数。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a machine or product that serves for years borrows the long line.
branches.cn: 器物线：能服役多年的机器或产品借用了那条长线。

branches.en: THE CULTURE: a book or custom outliving its time shows staying power.
branches.cn: 文化线：比自己时代活得更久的书或习俗体现出持久力。

branches.en: THE CAREER: a long life and a long stay in one post are praised with one word.
branches.cn: 职场线：长寿与在同一职位长期任职，都用同一个词来称赞。

intro.en: Longevity is a learned borrowing built from two Latin roots, long- and aev-, with only a few rare English derivatives.
intro.cn: longevity 是借用自拉丁语的书面词，由 long- 与 aev- 两个拉丁词根构成，英语里派生词很少。

latinIntro.en: Latin longus, long, and aevum, age or lifetime, compound in the adjective longaevus and its noun longaevitas.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 longus（长）与 aevum（年龄、一生）在形容词 longaevus 与名词 longaevitas 中合成。

items.example: The first root supplies the long span of time.
items.exampleCN: 第一个词根提供时间上的「长」。

items.example: The second root supplies the idea of a lifetime.
items.exampleCN: 第二个词根提供「一生」的概念。

items.example: The adjective joins the two roots into one word.
items.exampleCN: longaevus 把两个词根合成一个形容词。

items.example: The abstract noun is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个抽象名词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms the abstract noun longevity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成抽象名词 longevity。

items.example: Longevity keeps the Latin noun sense.
items.exampleCN: longevity 保留了拉丁名词的含义。

items.example: Longevous is the rare adjective of the family.
items.exampleCN: longevous 是这一词族里罕见的形容词。

items.example: The older form longaeval keeps the ae of the Latin spelling.
items.exampleCN: 较老的写法 longaeval 保留了拉丁拼写中的 ae。

items.example: It shares the age root aev- with the first word of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它同样含有表示「时代」的 aev- 词根。

definition_zh: 虱子；寄生于人或动物的虱；蚜虫等小害虫；（俚）卑鄙小人
definition_en: a small wingless insect that lives on the skin and hair of people or animals and feeds on blood, and by extension a similar tiny pest or a mean person
core_image: 一只米粒大的扁虫，用爪子死死钩住头发，把嘴刺进头皮
scene: 教室里铃声刚响，几个孩子又开始抓头发、挠耳朵。The school nurse checked every child for a louse after two cases were reported.
sceneCN: 这里 louse 是「虱子」（第 1 个义项：寄生在人和动物毛发皮肤上吸血的小虫）；句意为报告两例之后，校医检查了每个孩子有没有虱子。

pos.zh: 虱子；寄生小虫；小害虫；（俚）卑鄙的人

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，原义「长虱子的」，引申为「糟糕的；差劲的」
由前缀 de-「除去」加本词构成，义为「除虱；消毒去虫」
由本词加 wort（草本植物）构成，义为「马先蒿」，一种寄生植物
由本词加副词 up 构成的短语动词，非正式用法，义为「把事情弄糟」

senses.title: A tiny blood-sucking insect
senses.definition: a very small flat insect without wings that lives on the skin or hair of people and animals and bites to drink blood
senses.definitionCN: 一种极小、扁平、无翅的昆虫，寄居在人和动物的皮肤或毛发上，咬人吸血
senses.example: A single louse can lay dozens of eggs in a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一只虱子一周就能产下几十个卵。
senses.why: The Old English noun lus named this exact insect, and the parasitic image at the centre of the word has never changed.
senses.whyCN: 古英语名词 lus 指的就是这种虫子，这个词最核心的意象从古至今一直是「寄生虫」。

senses.title: Any small parasitic pest
senses.definition: a small insect that infests and damages plants, especially an aphid or a similar plant-sucking pest
senses.definitionCN: 侵害植物的微小昆虫，尤指蚜虫等吸食植物汁液的害虫
senses.example: Gardeners call the green louse on roses by its scientific name.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺师用学名来称呼玫瑰花上的绿色蚜虫。
senses.why: Because the insect is tiny and lives off its host, any plant-sucking pest gets the same parasitic label.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种虫子既小又靠寄主为生，所以任何吸食植物的害虫都被贴上同样的「寄生虫」标签。

senses.title: A contemptible person
senses.definition: an unpleasant or dishonest person who causes trouble for others, used as an insult
senses.definitionCN: 令人讨厌或不诚实、给别人添麻烦的人，用作侮辱性称呼
senses.example: He called the thief a louse for stealing from the poor.
senses.exampleCN: 他骂那个小偷卑鄙，竟去偷穷人的东西。
senses.why: A human parasite is imagined as an insect that clings to a host and lives off it, so dishonesty takes the insect form.
senses.whyCN: 人类中的寄生虫被想象成附着于寄主、靠它活命的虫子，于是不诚实的人就披上了虫子的外形。

senses.title: Sea louse, the rock-slater
senses.titleCN: （古称）海虱：潮间带的小型甲壳类
senses.definition: a small crustacean, especially a sea slater or related isopod, that scurries across rocks on the shore
senses.definitionCN: 一种小型甲壳类动物，尤指海潮虫等与等足类有关的动物，在岸边石缝间快步爬行
senses.example: Children turned over stones to look at a sea louse.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们翻开石头，去看来来去去的海虱。
senses.why: Fishermen and shore-dwellers lent the name to any little crawling creature that looks and moves like the parasite.
senses.whyCN: 渔民和海边居民把名字借给了任何一种外形与动作都像寄生虫的小爬虫。

senses.title: To clean lice out of hair or clothing
senses.definition: to remove lice from a person, an animal or clothing, now usually by the longer verb delouse
senses.definitionCN: 替人或动物、衣物清除虱子，如今通常用更长的动词 delouse
senses.example: Nurses used to louse the children every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 过去护士每年秋天都要给孩子们除虱。
senses.why: The noun is used directly as a verb, turning the parasite into an action: to louse someone is to find and remove the pest.
senses.whyCN: 名词被直接拿来当动词用，把寄生虫变成一种动作：给某人除虱，就是找出并清除这种害虫。

intro.en: Louse is one of the words English has always had, from Old English lus; its plural lice is also the old English plural.
intro.cn: louse 是英语自古就有的词，来自古英语 lus；复数 lice 同样保留了古时的复数形式。

items.en: The reconstructed form lus- names the parasite in early Germanic speech.
items.cn: 一般认为日耳曼语早期的重构形式 lus- 就指这种寄生虫。

items.en: Lus is recorded with the plural lys, later replaced by the old mutation plural.
items.cn: 古英语 lus 有记载，复数曾作 lys，后来被旧式的元音变音复数取代。

items.en: Middle English lous and the irregular plural lis keep the insect sense.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 lous，复数用不规则形式 lis，虫义不变。

items.en: The modern spellings louse and lice take their shape, with the same long vowel.
items.cn: 现代拼写 louse 与 lice 定型，两者保持同一个长元音。

items.en: The noun becomes a verb and the insulting human sense becomes common.
items.cn: 名词转成动词，「用来说人」的侮辱义也变得常见。

items.en: Modern usage names many similar pests: head louse, crab louse, sea louse and plant louse.
items.cn: 现代用法给许多相似的害虫命名：头虱、阴虱、海虱和植物蚜虫。

note.en: The first group gathers the English family and an old spelling; the second gathers other small pests and the words for dealing with them.
note.cn: 第一组收英语同族词与一个旧拼写；第二组收其他小型害虫以及与之相关的词。

entries.definition: The adjective formed from louse, originally infested with lice and now usually meaning very bad.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，由 louse 加后缀构成，本义「长虱子的」，如今多表示「糟糕的」。

entries.definition: The verb built with de- meaning to remove lice from a person or a place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，由 de-「除去」加 louse 构成，义为「除虱」。

entries.definition: Not tight or not fixed; it looks almost the same but has a different vowel and another origin.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「松的、松开的」；只是拼写相近，元音不同且词源不同。

entries.definition: A small jumping insect that bites people and animals without living on them.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「跳蚤」，咬人畜吸血但不在身上长住的小虫。

entries.definition: A tiny blood-sucking creature with eight legs that clings to skin and stays attached.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蜱虫」，八条腿、吸血并长时间叮在皮肤上的微小生物。

entries.definition: The eggs of lice, stuck to hair and the usual sign that someone is infested.
entries.definitionCN: 复数，义为「虱卵」，粘在头发上，常是头上有虱的迹象。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English source, the irregular plural, the family and the common compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的古英语来源、不规则复数、同族词以及常见复合词。

normal.en: The plural is lice, not louses, so remember louse as a single bug and lice as a whole colony.
normal.cn: 复数是不规则变化，词尾变成 -i- 的 lice 而不是直接加 -s 的写法；记住单数是一只，复数是一窝。

normal.en: The same irregular pattern appears in mouse and mice.
normal.cn: 同样的不规则复数也出现在 mouse 与 mice 这一组里。

normal.en: Louse plus -y gives lousy, which began as full of lice and ended up meaning bad.
normal.cn: louse 加后缀 -y 得到 lousy，本来指「满是虱子」，后来引申为「糟糕的」。

normal.en: Head lice spread mostly by direct head contact, not by cleanliness.
normal.cn: 头虱主要靠头部直接接触传播，与是否干净关系不大。

normal.en: Compare flea: a flea jumps away, a louse stays and holds on.
normal.cn: 对比 flea：跳蚤会跳着跑开，虱子则用爪子牢牢挂住不走。

abstract.en: Picture a grain of rice clinging to a single strand of hair.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒米大小的东西紧紧贴在一根头发上。

abstract.en: Imagine the same grain sitting on a rose leaf and drawing sap instead of blood.
abstract.cn: 再想象同样一粒东西趴在玫瑰叶上，吸的是汁液而不是血。
