abstract.en: See a crowd member leaning on someone else and making them carry the cost.
abstract.cn: 想象人群里有个人靠着别人过日子、让别人替自己承担，这就是骂人的 louse。

examples.en: The nurse found a louse behind the boy left ear.
examples.cn: 校医在男孩左耳后面发现了一只虱子。

examples.en: Aphids, the plant lice, weaken rose bushes in warm weather.
examples.cn: 蚜虫即植物虱子，在天气温暖时会削弱玫瑰丛。

examples.en: Only a louse would spread such a hurtful rumour.
examples.cn: 只有卑鄙小人才会散播这么伤人的谣言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「唠死」——唠唠叨叨贴着人不放，像虱子一样粘人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 lus「虱子」，一般认为源自日耳曼语重构形式 lus-，与德语 Laus、荷兰语 luis 同源；复数 lice 沿用古英语的元音变音复数，形似 mouse 与 mice 的对应，核心义「贴身吸血的小寄生虫」。

sensesIntro.en: Louse starts with the parasite itself, spreads the tiny-pest label to plants and shore animals, and finally turns the parasite into an insult and into an action.
sensesIntro.cn: louse 从虱子本身出发，把「小寄生虫」的标签扩展到植物害虫与海边小甲壳类，最后把寄生虫变成骂人话，并转成动词表示除虱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat insect the size of a grain of rice grips the hair and pierces the scalp.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只米粒大小的扁虫死死钩住头发，把嘴刺进头皮。

branches.en: THE HAIR: the human head louse is the oldest and clearest sense.
branches.cn: 毛发线：头虱是最古老、最清楚的义项。

branches.en: THE PLANT: any tiny sap-sucking pest takes the name.
branches.cn: 植物线：任何微小的吸汁害虫都接过这个名字。

branches.en: THE SHORE: a crawling crustacean is named by its insect look.
branches.cn: 海岸线：一种爬行甲壳类因外形像虫而得名。

branches.en: THE INSULT: a dishonest person is imagined as a human parasite.
branches.cn: 骂人线：不诚实的人被想象成人身上的寄生虫。

branches.en: THE ACTION: the noun itself becomes a verb for clearing the pest away.
branches.cn: 动作线：名词本身转成动词，表示把害虫清除掉。

intro.en: Louse is a native English word of Germanic origin, so no Latin root lies behind it; English builds its small family with native suffixes.
intro.cn: louse 是源自日耳曼语的英语本族词，背后并没有拉丁词根，英语用本族后缀为它扩展出小小的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin has its own unrelated word pediculus for the louse, with derivatives such as pediculosis, but it is not the source of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用另一个无关的词 pediculus 表示虱子，并派生 pediculosis（虱病），但它并不是英语 louse 的来源。

items.example: The Old English noun is the direct source of the modern word.
items.exampleCN: 古英语名词是现代词的直接来源。

items.example: The old spelling lus shows the short stem of the word.
items.exampleCN: 古拼写 lus 显示了这个词的短词干。

items.example: Lice keeps the old vowel change of the Germanic plural.
items.exampleCN: lice 保留了日耳曼语复数的旧元音变化。

items.example: The suffix -y forms lousy from louse.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把 louse 变成 lousy。

items.example: Lousy shows the jump from insect to insult.
items.exampleCN: lousy 展示了从虫子义跳到贬义的过程。

items.example: The prefix de- in delouse means removal.
items.exampleCN: delouse 中的前缀 de- 表示「除去」。

items.example: Delouse is the common modern verb for the action.
items.exampleCN: delouse 是这个动作常见的现代动词。

items.example: The compound joins louse with wort, the old word for a plant.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把 louse 与表示草本植物的古词 wort 连在一起。

latinEntries.example: It is the Latin name for the insect, not the source of the English word.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是这种虫子的拉丁名，并非英语词的来源。

latinEntries.example: Medical Latin builds this term on the Latin name for the louse.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 医学拉丁语用「虱子」的拉丁名构成这个术语。

definition_zh: 润滑剂；润滑油；（比喻）缓和关系、减少摩擦的因素
definition_en: a substance such as oil or grease that you put between moving surfaces to reduce friction, or anything that makes interaction smoother
core_image: 两只咬合的齿轮之间被抹上一层油，转动时不再发涩发响
scene: 自行车链条干涩发响，修车师傅拧开小瓶，在每一节链环上滴油。A few drops of lubricant quietened the grinding pedals within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 lubricant 是「润滑剂」（第 1 个义项：减少机械摩擦的油或脂）；句意为几滴润滑油几分钟内就让吱嘎作响的踏板安静下来。

pos.zh: 润滑剂；润滑油；起缓和作用的因素
润滑用的；有润滑作用的（较少见）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词根 lubric- 加动词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「给……加润滑油；润滑」
由动词 lubricate 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「润滑；润滑作用」
由同一拉丁词根加形容词后缀构成，义为「滑腻的；淫荡的」，语义偏离机械用法
由拉丁词根加名词后缀构成，义为「润滑性；滑溜；善变」

senses.title: A substance that reduces friction
senses.definition: a substance such as oil, grease or graphite placed between two surfaces to reduce friction and wear
senses.definitionCN: 放在两个表面之间以减少摩擦力与磨损的物质，如油、脂或石墨
senses.example: Apply a little lubricant to the hinge once a month.
senses.exampleCN: 每个月在合页上抹一点润滑剂。
senses.why: Latin lubricare means to make slippery, and the -ant ending names the thing that does it, so a lubricant is a slipperiness-making substance.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 lubricare 意为「使光滑」，后缀 -ant 指做这件事的东西，所以 lubricant 就是让表面变滑的物质。

senses.title: A body fluid that eases movement
senses.definition: a natural fluid, such as synovial fluid in a joint or tears on the eye, that keeps tissue moving smoothly
senses.definitionCN: 关节滑液、眼泪等天然液体，使组织运动顺滑
senses.example: Healthy joints produce their own natural lubricant.
senses.exampleCN: 健康的关节会自己产生天然的润滑液。
senses.why: The same slippery film works inside a living body, where fluid between bones does the job of the oil between gears.
senses.whyCN: 同一层滑膜也作用于活体之内：骨头之间的液体承担着齿轮之间机油的作用。

senses.title: Something that eases a relationship
senses.titleCN: （比喻）缓和关系、减少摩擦的因素
senses.definition: figuratively, anything such as money, humour or courtesy that makes dealings between people go more smoothly
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指金钱、幽默或礼貌等使人与人之间的往来更顺畅的东西
senses.example: Good humour is a useful lubricant in long negotiations.
senses.exampleCN: 在漫长的谈判中，好心情是很有用的润滑剂。
senses.why: Social friction is pictured exactly like metal friction, so anything that eases contact between people counts as a lubricant.
senses.whyCN: 人际摩擦被想象成金属摩擦，于是任何能让彼此接触更顺滑的东西，都算得上 lubricant。

senses.title: Lubricant oil in a machine system
senses.definition: a branded or technical oil or grease product designed for engines, gears or tools and sold for maintenance
senses.definitionCN: 专为发动机、齿轮或工具设计、作为保养用品出售的油品或润滑脂商品
senses.example: The shop stocks several lubricants for bike chains.
senses.exampleCN: 店里有好几种供自行车链条使用的润滑油。
senses.why: Once the substance becomes an industry, the plural names the packaged products rather than any single drop.
senses.whyCN: 当这种物质成为一个产业，复数形式就指一罐罐商品，而不是任何单独的一滴。

senses.title: Describing a lubricating substance or effect
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe a fluid, surface or action that lubricates
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，描述具有润滑作用的液体、表面或动作
senses.example: The lubricant film protects the metal parts from rust.
senses.exampleCN: 这层润滑油膜保护金属零件不生锈。
senses.why: The -ant form is also a participle-like adjective, so it can sit before a noun and describe the slippery film itself.
senses.whyCN: -ant 形式同时是近似分词的形容词，能放在名词前描述那层滑腻的油膜。

intro.en: Lubricant comes from Latin lubricans, the present participle of lubricare, to make slippery, which relates to lubricus, slippery.
intro.cn: lubricant 来自拉丁语 lubricans，是 lubricare（使光滑）的现在分词，与 lubricus（滑的）有关。

items.en: Lubricus means slippery, and lubricare means to make slippery.
items.cn: lubricus 意为「滑的」，lubricare 意为「使光滑」。

items.en: Lubricans is the present participle, the one making slippery.
items.cn: lubricans 是现在分词，指「使变滑的那种东西」。

items.en: The verb lubricate enters English first, with a figurative sense of easing things.
items.cn: 动词 lubricate 先进入英语，最初多用于比喻意义上的缓和。

items.en: With industrial machinery, lubricant becomes a standard noun for the oil or grease.
items.cn: 随着工业机械兴起，lubricant 成为指油或脂的标准名词。

items.en: Modern usage keeps the mechanical, medical and figurative senses side by side.
items.cn: 现代用法让机械义、生理义与比喻义并存。

note.en: The first group gathers the verb family and near spellings; the second gathers related substances and the idea of slipping easily.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的动词与形近词；第二组收相关物质与「容易打滑」的概念。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to put oil or grease on something so that it moves more easily.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「给……加润滑油、润滑」。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or process of adding a lubricant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「润滑、润滑作用」，指添加润滑剂的行为或过程。

entries.definition: An adjective from the same root meaning slippery or lewd rather than technical.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，与 lubricant 同根，但义为「滑腻的、淫荡的」，不走技术路线。

entries.definition: A thick oily substance used on machines, but also the household cooking fat.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「润滑脂」，在机器上使用，但也可指厨房里的油脂。

entries.definition: A general liquid that can be fuel, food or lubricant depending on the context.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「油」，可作燃料、食用油或润滑油，要由语境确定。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a surface that is hard to grip, the quality a lubricant produces.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「滑的、难抓住的」，正是润滑剂造成的性质。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb, the -ant and -ate family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁动词、-ant 与 -ate 词族，以及这个词真正出现的搭配。

normal.en: Lubric- plus -ant: the thing that makes surfaces slippery.
normal.cn: lubric- 加 -ant：让表面变滑的那件东西。

normal.en: The verb lubricate uses -ate: to perform the action of oiling.
normal.cn: 动词 lubricate 用 -ate：执行上油这个动作。

normal.en: The noun lubrication uses -ion: the act or result of oiling.
normal.cn: 名词 lubrication 用 -ion：上油这个动作或其结果。

normal.en: Compare greasy: grease is the substance, lubricant is the product category sold for machines.
normal.cn: 对比 greasy：grease 常指黏稠的油脂，lubricant 则是为机器出售的「润滑油品」类别。

normal.en: A lubricant acts as a film: it separates two surfaces so they slide instead of scraping.
normal.cn: lubricant 起油膜作用：把两个表面隔开，让它们滑动而不是互相刮擦。

abstract.en: Picture two metal gears with a thin golden film of oil between their teeth.
abstract.cn: 想象两只金属齿轮，齿与齿之间隔着一层薄薄的金色油膜。

abstract.en: See a knee joint where clear fluid lets bone ends glide without grinding.
abstract.cn: 想想膝关节，透明液体让骨端彼此滑过去，而不是硬磨。

abstract.en: Bring the film into a tense meeting: a joke greases the talk the way oil greases a hinge.
abstract.cn: 把这层油膜带进一场紧张的会议：一句玩笑就像给合页上油一样，让谈话顺滑起来。

examples.en: The mechanic applied a thick lubricant to the door hinges.
examples.cn: 修理工在门合页上抹了厚厚一层润滑剂。

examples.en: Without lubricant, the bearings screech and wear out quickly.
examples.cn: 没有润滑油，轴承会尖叫并迅速磨损。

examples.en: Shared coffee is a quiet lubricant for a long staff meeting.
examples.cn: 共用一壶咖啡，是漫长员工会议里一种安静的润滑剂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撸布里肯」——撸上一把油，布里也肯滑着走：润滑剂；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 lubricus「滑的」→ lubricare「使光滑、润滑」→ 现在分词 lubricans → 英语名词 lubricant「润滑剂」，同一词根还生出 lubricate、lubrication 与 lubricious，核心义「让接触面变滑的那层东西」。

sensesIntro.en: Lubricant names the slippery substance itself, then the body fluid that does the same job, the figurative thing that eases people, the packaged product and finally the attributive use before a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: lubricant 先指让表面变滑的物质，再指体内起同样作用的液体、比喻中缓和人际的事物、成罐出售的油品，最后用作名词前的定语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin film of oil lies between two gears that turn without grinding.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只咬合的齿轮之间抹上一层油，转动时不再发涩发响。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: oil or grease between metal parts is the central sense.
branches.cn: 机械线：金属零件之间的油或脂是核心义项。

branches.en: THE BODY: the same film appears as fluid inside joints and eyes.
branches.cn: 身体线：同一层油膜出现在关节与眼睛里的液体上。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: humour or courtesy lowers social friction the way oil lowers metal friction.
branches.cn: 人际线：幽默或礼貌像油降低金属摩擦一样，降低人际摩擦。

branches.en: THE SHELF: bottles and tins of oil are sold as products.
branches.cn: 货架线：瓶装罐装的油作为商品出售。

branches.en: THE FILM: the same word sits before a noun to describe the protective coat.
branches.cn: 油膜线：同一个词放在名词前，描述那层保护膜。

intro.en: Lubricant joins a Latin slipping root with the English ending -ant; the verb lubricate and the nouns lubrication and lubricity grow around it.
intro.cn: lubricant 由拉丁文中表示「打滑」的词根与英语词尾 -ant 构成，周围还长出动词 lubricate 与名词 lubrication、lubricity。

latinIntro.en: Latin lubricus, slippery, and lubricare, to make slippery, are both recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lubricus（滑的）与 lubricare（使光滑）均有文献记录，只有更早的印欧语来源存疑。

items.example: The root carries the idea of a surface that slips.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载「表面打滑」的意思。

items.example: The adjective is the oldest member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是这一词族中最古老的成员。

items.example: The verb supplies the action behind the English nouns.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了英语名词背后的动作。

items.meaning: the thing that does an action
items.example: The suffix -ant forms lubricant from the participle.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 由分词构成 lubricant。

items.example: It forms lubricate.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 lubricate。

items.example: It forms lubrication.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 lubrication。

items.example: It forms lubricity.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 lubricity。

items.example: It forms lubricious.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 lubricious。

items.example: Lubricant keeps the technical sense of the Latin participle.
items.exampleCN: lubricant 保留了拉丁分词的技术含义。

latinEntries.example: The participle supplies the shape of the English noun.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个分词提供了英语名词的词形。

definition_zh: 给……加润滑油；使润滑；使顺利进行
definition_en: to put oil or grease on something so that its parts move easily, or to make a process run more smoothly
core_image: 往吱吱作响的轴心倒油，原先干涩咬滞的转轮立刻轻快旋动
scene: 车轮很久没有保养，推一下便发出刺耳的吱嘎声。A few drops of oil will lubricate the axle and stop that awful noise.
sceneCN: 这里 lubricate 是「给机械加润滑油」（第 1 个义项：在部件表面加油脂以减少摩擦）；句意：滴几滴油就能润滑车轴，止住那可怕的响声。图中可辨识物件：油壶、滴油、车轮。

pos.zh: 动词：给机器或部件加润滑油、减少摩擦；比喻使事情顺利进行

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「润滑；加油」
由动词词干加后缀 -ant 构成，义为「润滑剂；润滑油」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「加了润滑油的」
与 lubricate 共享拉丁词根，义为「滑溜的；油滑的」

senses.title: To apply oil or grease to moving parts
senses.definition: to put oil or grease on the parts of a machine so that they slide over each other more easily
senses.definitionCN: 在机器部件上涂油或油脂，使它们相互滑动得更省力
senses.example: Mechanics lubricate the gears before every race.
senses.exampleCN: 机械师在每场比赛前都给齿轮加润滑油。
senses.why: The Latin verb lubricare means to make slippery, so the basic scene is oil poured between two surfaces that rub.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 lubricare 意为使滑溜，所以最基本的场景就是在相互摩擦的两个表面之间倒上油，让它们滑起来。

senses.title: To make a joint or tissue flexible
senses.definition: to keep a joint or body tissue moist and flexible so that it moves without friction or stiffness
senses.definitionCN: 保持关节或身体组织湿润灵活，使活动时没有摩擦和僵硬感
senses.example: The knee joint is lubricated by a natural fluid called synovial fluid.
senses.exampleCN: 膝关节由一种叫做滑液的天然液体润滑。
senses.why: The body does for its joints what a mechanic does for a bearing: a fluid film carries the same slippery image inside the body.
senses.whyCN: 身体为关节所做的，正如机械师为轴承所做的：一层液膜把同样「滑」的意象带进了身体内部。

senses.title: To coat a surface so things may slip
senses.definition: to make a surface smooth or slippery by covering it with oil, grease, or another substance
senses.definitionCN: 用油、油脂或其他物质覆盖表面，使之平滑或滑溜
senses.example: Rain had lubricated the cobbles, and every step was a risk.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水把鹅卵石路面变得湿滑，每走一步都有风险。
senses.why: Here the word is bent slightly against its usual purpose: the same oily film that frees a wheel also takes away traction.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词稍稍偏离了它通常的目的：同一层油膜既能让轮子转动自如，也会夺走脚下的抓地力。

senses.title: To make a process run smoothly
senses.definition: to make a process, negotiation, or conversation work with less tension and fewer obstacles
senses.definitionCN: 使流程、谈判或交谈减少摩擦与阻碍，进行得更顺畅
senses.example: A little humour can lubricate even the stiffest of meetings.
senses.exampleCN: 一点幽默能让最僵硬的会议也顺畅起来。
senses.why: The physical part of the metaphor is kept while the object changes from metal to people, and friction becomes social tension.
senses.whyCN: 比喻保留了「物理上的滑」这一部分，只是对象从金属换成了人，摩擦也就变成了人际间的紧张。

senses.title: Formal: to ease the passing of something
senses.definition: to help the passage of ideas, words, or money go more easily, in formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文体中帮助思想、言辞或钱财更顺利地流通
senses.example: Cheap credit had lubricated the wheels of trade for years.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价信贷多年来一直使贸易的车轮运转顺畅。
senses.why: This formal use pushes the image furthest inside a system, where oil stands for money or words and a wheel stands for the whole economy or debate.
senses.whyCN: 这一正式用法把意象推到了系统内部的最远处：油代表金钱或言辞，车轮代表整个经济或辩论。

senses.title: Figurative: to smooth over an awkward moment
senses.definition: to soften an awkward or tense situation with words or action so that people stay comfortable
senses.definitionCN: 用言语或行动缓和尴尬、紧张的局面，使大家保持自在
senses.example: He told a quick joke to lubricate the awkward silence that followed.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲了个简短的笑话，缓和了随后出现的尴尬沉默。
senses.why: Silence is imagined as a dry, grinding gap between two speakers, and a joke is the oil that makes it pass without squeaking.
senses.whyCN: 沉默被想象成两人之间一个干涩、摩擦的缝隙，而一个笑话就是让这道缝隙不再吱嘎作响的油。

senses.title: Technical: to add fluid before or during use
senses.definition: to treat a device, seal, or material with a fluid before or during use so that it operates without wear
senses.definitionCN: 在使用前或使用过程中用流体处理器械、密封件或材料，使其运转时不磨损
senses.example: The seal must be lubricated with clean oil before it is fitted.
senses.exampleCN: 安装前必须用洁净的机油润滑密封件。
senses.why: Engineering splits the general act into stages: priming with fluid is called pre-lubrication, and oiling at intervals is called routine lubrication.
senses.whyCN: 工程学把一般动作分成步骤：用流体预处理叫预润滑，间隔注油叫例行润滑。

senses.title: Humorous: to encourage the flow of drink
senses.definition: to help people talk more freely by giving them a little alcohol, used in a joking tone
senses.definitionCN: 用一点酒使人更健谈，带有开玩笑的语气
senses.example: Let us lubricate the conversation with a glass of wine.
senses.exampleCN: 咱们来杯葡萄酒，让谈话顺滑起来。
senses.why: The playful use returns to a fluid, but now the fluid is inside the drinkers rather than between metal parts.
senses.whyCN: 这一俏皮用法又回到了「液体」，只是这次的液体不在金属之间，而在喝酒的人体内。

intro.en: Lubricate comes from Latin lubricare, to make slippery, from lubricus, slippery, a word older than any Latin we can trace with certainty.
intro.cn: lubricate 来自拉丁语 lubricare（使滑溜），源于 lubricus（滑的）；这一组词在拉丁语中的更早来源已不明确。

items.en: Lubricus, slippery, is generally linked by scholars to a root meaning to slip or glide, but the reconstruction is uncertain.
items.cn: lubricus 意为「滑的」，学界一般认为它与「滑倒、滑动」的词根有关，但这一重构形式并不确定。

items.en: Lubricus describes anything slippery, and crucially the idea of slipperiness as something that can be given or taken away.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lubricus 描述任何滑溜之物，关键之处在于「滑」被视为可以被给予、也可以被收回的状态。

items.en: The verb lubricare means to make slippery, to oil, or to cause to slip.
items.cn: 动词 lubricare 意为使滑溜、上油，或使打滑。

items.en: The adjective lubricus also carries a moral sense, slippery in speech or conduct, as in the later English word lubricious.
items.cn: 形容词 lubricus 还带有道德含义，指言谈行为上的「油滑」，这也延续到后来的英语词 lubricious。

items.en: English borrows lubricare and lubricus through learned Latin, at first in medical and technical writing.
items.cn: 英语经由书本拉丁语借入 lubricare 与 lubricus，最初出现在医学与技术写作中。

items.en: Industrial English turns lubrication into a science, and figurative uses spread the word to meetings, markets, and conversations.
items.cn: 现代英语把润滑变成一门科学，比喻用法又把这个词推广到会议、市场与日常交谈。

note.en: Lubricate belongs to the Latin slippery family and sits close to words for oiling, greasing, and easing.
note.cn: lubricate 属于拉丁语「滑」词族，与表示上油、涂脂、使缓和的词义很接近。

entries.definitionCN: 润滑；加油

entries.definition: slippery, or lewd in a suggestive way
entries.definitionCN: 滑溜的；油滑不端的

normalIntro.en: Lubricate is a mechanic word first: oil at the point of friction turns a dry grind into a clean glide.
normalIntro.cn: lubricate 先是机械语境里的词：在摩擦点上油，让干涩的磨擦变成顺畅的滑行。

normal.en: Lubricate shares its Latin root with lubricant and lubricious.
normal.cn: lubricate 与 lubricant、lubricious 共享拉丁词根「滑」。

normal.en: The past form lubricated often becomes an adjective before a noun.
normal.cn: 过去分词 lubricated 常转作形容词放在名词前使用。

normal.en: Well lubricated means running smoothly with little friction.
normal.cn: well lubricated 表示运转顺畅、摩擦极小。

normal.en: Lubrication system is the engineering phrase for the oiling parts of an engine.
normal.cn: lubrication system 是工程学中表示发动机注油部件的说法。

normal.en: Compare lubricate with grease: grease blocks moisture, lubricate simply reduces friction.
normal.cn: 对比同义的 grease：grease 还含防潮之意，lubricate 只强调减少摩擦。

abstract.en: Picture one drop of oil falling on a dry axle and spreading in a slow silver ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴油落在干涩的轴上，缓缓摊开成一圈银光。

abstract.en: Picture a knee bending without a sound, as if a hinge had been oiled inside.
abstract.cn: 想象膝盖弯下时毫无声响，仿佛里头的合页刚刚上了油。

abstract.en: Picture a room where a joke is the only thing that keeps silence from squeaking.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子人，唯有一个笑话让沉默不至于吱嘎作响。

examples.en: You should lubricate the hinges twice a year.
examples.cn: 铰链应该每年润滑两次。

examples.en: The machine was well lubricated and ran almost silently.
examples.cn: 这台机器润滑良好，运转时几乎没有声音。

examples.en: The two governments used small trade deals to lubricate the talks.
examples.cn: 两国政府用一些小型贸易协议让谈判顺畅进行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「鲁布瑞克」——录音带卡住，涂上蜡就滑顺了：润滑。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 lubricus（滑的）→ lubricare（使滑溜、上油）→ 英语 lubricate（润滑），核心义「让摩擦的两个面滑起来」。

sensesIntro.en: Lubricate begins with oiling metal, passes through joints, surfaces and processes, and ends with the mild figurative and humorous uses of modern English.
sensesIntro.cn: lubricate 从给金属上油开始，经过关节、表面与流程，最后落到现代英语里略带比喻和玩笑色彩的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: oil poured between two surfaces that rub, so they glide instead of grinding.
core.cn: 核心意象：油倒在两个相互摩擦的表面之间，让它们滑行而非研磨。

branches.en: MACHINE: oil on moving parts is the literal, mechanic core.
branches.cn: 机械线：给运动部件上油是最实在的核心义。

branches.en: BODY AND SURFACE: joints and wet stones carry the same slippery film outside the workshop.
branches.cn: 身体与表面线：关节和湿滑路面把同一层油膜带出了车间。

branches.en: PROCESS: a meeting, a market, or a trade becomes a mechanism that oil keeps running.
branches.cn: 流程线：会议、市场或贸易变成了靠油维持运转的机械。

branches.en: SOCIAL: silence or awkwardness is treated as a dry gap that oil can close.
branches.cn: 社交线：沉默与尴尬被当作一道干涩的缝隙，靠「油」来弥合。

branches.en: TECHNIQUE AND FUN: staged oiling in engineering and a glass of wine both return to the plainest fluid.
branches.cn: 技术与玩笑线：工程的分步注油和一杯酒都回到了最朴素的液体。

intro.en: Lubricate is built from the Latin root lubric- plus the verb ending -ate, with nouns and adjectives in the same family.
intro.cn: lubricate 由拉丁词根 lubric- 加动词词尾 -ate 构成，同一词族里还有名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin lubricus means slippery, and lubricare means to make slippery or to oil.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lubricus 意为滑的，lubricare 意为使滑溜或上油。

items.example: The root lubric carries the idea of slipperiness.
items.exampleCN: 词根 lubric 承载「滑」的意思。

items.example: The ending -ate turns the root into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 把词根变成动词。

items.example: Lubricus describes a greasy surface.
items.exampleCN: lubricus 描述油滑的表面。

items.example: Lubricare is the direct ancestor of the verb.
items.exampleCN: lubricare 是这个动词的直接前身。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion gives lubrication.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 lubrication。

items.example: Lubrication is the process itself.
items.exampleCN: lubrication 指润滑这一过程。

items.meaningCN: 表示执行动作之物的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ant gives lubricant.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 构成 lubricant。

items.example: A lubricant is the oil, not the action.
items.exampleCN: lubricant 指油本身，而不是动作。

items.example: The suffix -ious gives lubricious.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ious 构成 lubricious。

items.example: Lubricious keeps the moral sense of the Latin.
items.exampleCN: lubricious 保留了拉丁语的道德含义。

definition_zh: 赚钱的；有利可图的；获利丰厚的
definition_en: producing a large amount of money or profit
core_image: 一只鼓胀的钱袋压在成交的账本上，数字一行行往上加
scene: 小镇的老码头被改造成游船停靠点，一年后的账本全是盈余。Cutting the old tariffs made the shipping business unusually lucrative.
sceneCN: 这里 lucrative 是「有利可图的」（第 1 个义项：能带来大笔金钱或利润）；句意：削减旧的关税让航运生意变得格外赚钱。图中可辨识物件：账本、钱袋、货船。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「有利可图地」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「获利性；赚钱程度」
与 lucrative 同源的拉丁名词，义为「钱财」（多含贬义）
语义相近的形容词，义为「金钱上的」

senses.title: Producing a good deal of money
senses.definition: producing a large amount of money or a high profit, especially for a business
senses.definitionCN: 能带来大笔金钱或高额利润，尤其指生意
senses.example: Consulting turned out to be far more lucrative than teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 事实证明，做咨询比教书赚钱得多。
senses.why: The Latin noun lucrum means gain or profit, and the adjective in -ive names whatever brings that gain.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 lucrum 意为收益、利润，带 -ive 的形容词就用来形容能带来这种收益的事物。

senses.title: Worth doing for the reward
senses.definition: repaying the effort or resources put into it, whether in money, power, or advantage
senses.definitionCN: 回报能够抵偿投入的努力与资源，无论是钱财、权力还是好处
senses.example: For him the long night shift was lucrative in status, if not in pay.
senses.exampleCN: 对他来说，长期上夜班在地位上是有回报的，尽管工钱并未增加。
senses.why: The same root idea widens from cash to any gain that makes an effort feel worth it.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「收益」的概念从现金扩展到任何让努力显得值得的好处。

senses.title: Describing a sum or property that yields income
senses.definition: describing a sum of money, property, or investment that regularly produces income
senses.definitionCN: 形容款项、财产或投资能定期产生收入
senses.example: The fund owns a lucrative block of offices in the city centre.
senses.exampleCN: 这只基金在市中心拥有一栋收益可观的写字楼。
senses.why: Here the adjective describes the thing that produces income rather than the person who receives it.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个形容词修饰的是产生收入的东西，而不是收取收入的人。

senses.title: Making a position or profession pay well
senses.definition: applied to a job, rank, or profession that pays whoever holds it very well
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容某个职位、级别或职业，给担任者的报酬很高
senses.example: He gave up a lucrative post in the ministry to run a rural school.
senses.exampleCN: 他放弃了部里一份收入丰厚的职位，去办一所乡村学校。
senses.why: The gain is attached to a role or rank, so the word shifts from the trade itself to the seat inside it.
senses.whyCN: 收益被附加在职位或级别上，于是这个词从行业本身转向了行业里的那把椅子。

senses.title: Describing a dishonest way to profit
senses.titleCN: （常含贬义）靠不正当手段捞钱的
senses.definition: used with a critical tone for profits that are gained dishonestly or harmfully
senses.definitionCN: 带批评语气，指靠不诚实或有害的方式获得利润
senses.example: The inquiry exposed a lucrative trade in forged certificates.
senses.exampleCN: 调查揭出了一桩伪造证书的暴利买卖。
senses.why: The root lucre already carries a taint, as in the biblical phrase filthy lucre, and that suspicion colours the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 词根 lucre 本身就带有一层污名，例如《圣经》里的「不义之财」一语，这种怀疑也染上了这个形容词。

senses.title: Objective, neutral use in finance
senses.definition: in neutral financial writing, describing deals or sectors that give strong returns on capital
senses.definitionCN: 在中立的财经写作中，形容交易或行业能给资本带来较高回报
senses.example: Renewable energy has become a lucrative sector for private investors.
senses.exampleCN: 对私人投资者而言，可再生能源已成为回报丰厚的行业。
senses.why: Stripped of judgment, the word simply reports a high return, which is why finance writing uses it so often.
senses.whyCN: 去掉价值判断之后，这个词只是客观报告高回报，这正是财经写作频繁使用它的原因。

senses.title: Doubtful: a deal that looks too good
senses.definition: describing a proposal that appears very profitable, often when the speaker is suspicious of it
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个看起来非常赚钱的提议，说话人往往对它心存怀疑
senses.example: They offered him a lucrative deal that nobody could quite explain.
senses.exampleCN: 他们向他提供了一笔没人说得清的有油水的交易。
senses.why: The adjective still reports profit, but the surrounding doubt adds an ironic edge to the very thing praised.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词仍然在说利润，但周围的怀疑给所称赞的东西加了一层反讽。

senses.title: Slightly old-fashioned: yielding due reward
senses.definition: in older writing, used of a course of action or study that brings a satisfying return
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧的文字里，用于形容某种行动或研究带来令人满意的回报
senses.example: A year in the archives proved a lucrative investment in knowledge.
senses.exampleCN: 在档案馆待上一年，证明是一项在知识上大有回报的投入。
senses.why: In older usage the profit was not only money but also learning or honour, before finance narrowed the word.
senses.whyCN: 在较早的用法中，这种「收益」不只是金钱，还包括学识或名誉，后来财经语境才把这个词的含义收窄了。

intro.en: Lucrative comes from Latin lucrari, to gain, and lucrum, gain or profit, probably from an older root for booty taken in war.
intro.cn: lucrative 来自拉丁语 lucrari（获利）与 lucrum（收益、利润），其更早来源大概是表示战利品的词根。

items.en: The recontructed root is generally tied to booty or spoils, which explains why gain was once a matter of capture.
items.cn: 所重构的词根一般与战利品、掠获物有关，这解释了为何「收益」最初是一种夺取之物。

items.en: Lucrum names gain, profit, or avarice, and the verb lucrari means to gain or to make a profit.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lucrum 指收益、利润或贪婪，动词 lucrari 意为获得、获利。

items.en: The adjective lucrativus describes what brings gain, and seeds the moral suspicion around lucre.
items.cn: 形容词 lucrativus 形容能带来收益之物，也为 lucre 周围埋下了道德上的疑虑。

items.en: English takes the word through legal and learned Latin as an adjective for profitable arrangements.
items.cn: 英语经由法律与书本拉丁语借入这个词，用作形容有利可图的安排。

items.en: The word enters ordinary commercial writing, and lucre survives beside it with a strongly negative tone.
items.cn: 这个词进入普通的商业写作，而 lucre 以强烈的贬义语气活在它旁边。

items.en: Today lucrative is the neutral word for high profit, and lucre is the judgemental one.
items.cn: 今天 lucrative 是中性的「高利润」，lucre 则是带评判色彩的「钱财」。

note.en: Lucrative shares its Latin root with lucre, and competes in meaning with the plainer words profitable and rewarding.
note.cn: lucrative 与 lucre 同出拉丁词根，并在意思上与更朴素的 profitable、rewarding 相互竞争。

entries.definition: money, especially as greedily gained
entries.definitionCN: 钱财；不义之财

entries.definition: in a money-making way
entries.definitionCN: 有利可图地

entries.definition: the quality of being profitable
entries.definitionCN: 获利性

entries.definition: clearness of thought, from a light root, only spelling similar
entries.definitionCN: 思维清晰，词根来自「光」，只是拼写相近而词源不同

entries.definition: making money or giving benefit
entries.definitionCN: 有利润的；有益的

entries.definition: well paid for work done
entries.definitionCN: 报酬丰厚的

entries.definition: giving satisfaction rather than money
entries.definitionCN: 有回报的；令人满足的

normalIntro.en: Lucrative is built on gain: whatever wears the word is making money or at least paying back the effort.
normalIntro.cn: lucrative 建立在「收益」之上：凡是带上这个词的东西都在赚钱，或至少能把投入赚回来。

normal.en: Lucrative keeps the same root as lucre, the old word for money.
normal.cn: lucrative 与表示钱财的旧词 lucre 共享同一个词根。

normal.en: The set phrase a lucrative business is the most natural collocation.
normal.cn: 固定说法 a lucrative business 是最自然的搭配。

normal.en: Long adjectives take more and most, so more lucrative is the usual comparative.
normal.cn: 长形容词用 more 和 most，所以常见比较级是 more lucrative。

normal.en: The adverb lucratively appears in finance writing.
normal.cn: 副词 lucratively 多出现在财经写作中。

normal.en: Compare lucrative with profitable: both rank money, but lucrative suggests a bigger gain.
normal.cn: 对比 profitable：两者都在衡量金钱，但 lucrative 暗示收益更大。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy coin bag with a ledger open on top of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沉重的钱袋，上面摊着打开的账本。

abstract.en: Picture the same set of numbers rising one line after another.
abstract.cn: 想象同一列数字一行接一行地往上冒。

abstract.en: Picture a deal that closes quietly, while someone in the room is uneasy.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔悄悄成交的生意，而屋里有人心里发毛。

examples.en: Tourism has proved highly lucrative for the small island.
examples.cn: 对一个如此小的岛屿来说，旅游业已经被证明利润丰厚。

examples.en: She left a secure job for a less lucrative career in publishing.
examples.cn: 她放弃了稳定的工作，转投回报较低的出版业生涯。

examples.en: The two firms signed a lucrative contract for airport maintenance.
examples.cn: 两家公司签下了一份利润丰厚的机场维护合同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卢克拉提夫」——账本往外「提」数，提得越多越赚钱：有利可图的。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 lucrum（收益、利润）→ lucrari（获利）→ lucrativus（能带来收益的）→ 英语 lucrative（赚钱的），核心是「带来增益」。

sensesIntro.en: Lucrative starts as a plain label for high profit, then widens to other rewards, shifts onto property and posts, takes on a critical tone, and finally narrows back into neutral finance.
sensesIntro.cn: lucrative 最初只是「高利润」的朴素标签，之后扩展到其他回报，再移到资产与职位上，带上批评语气，最后又收拢回中性的财经用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a swollen money bag resting on a closed ledger, profit written line by line.
core.cn: 核心意象：鼓胀的钱袋压着合上的账本，利润一行行写满。

branches.en: TRADE: a business or trade that earns well is the plainest sense.
branches.cn: 生意线：赚钱的买卖是最朴素的义项。

branches.en: REWARD: the profit may be learning, status, or honour rather than cash.
branches.cn: 回报线：收益也可以是学识、地位或名誉，而非现金。

branches.en: THINGS AND SEATS: property yields income, and a post pays whoever holds it.
branches.cn: 资产与职位线：财产产生收入，职位给担任者带来报酬。

branches.en: SUSPICION: gain with a taint, or a deal that seems too good, keeps the old edge of lucre.
branches.cn: 怀疑线：带污点的收益，或好得可疑的交易，保留了 lucre 的旧锋芒。

branches.en: FINANCE: stripped of judgement, the word reports a strong return on capital.
branches.cn: 财经线：去掉评判之后，这个词只是报告资本的高回报。

intro.en: Lucrative is an adjective built on the Latin profit root lucr- with the suffix -ative.
intro.cn: lucrative 是由拉丁词根 lucr- 加形容词词尾 -ative 构成的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin lucrum means gain or profit, and lucrari means to gain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lucrum 意为收益或利润，lucrari 意为获得。

items.example: The root lucr- carries the idea of gain.
items.exampleCN: 词根 lucr- 承载「收益」的意思。

items.meaning: tending to, having the nature of
items.example: The suffix -ative makes an adjective of tendency.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ative 构成表示倾向的形容词。

items.example: Lucrum is the direct source of the root.
items.exampleCN: lucrum 是这一词根的直接来源。

items.example: Lucrari supplies the verbal idea behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: lucrari 提供形容词背后的动作概念。

items.example: Lucrativus is the form English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: lucrativus 是英语借入的形式。

items.example: Lucre keeps the unfiltered root sense.
items.exampleCN: lucre 保留了未经修饰的词根义。

items.example: The suffix -ly gives lucratively.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 lucratively。

items.example: The suffix -ness gives lucrativeness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 lucrativeness。

items.example: Lucratively modifies how profit is made.
items.exampleCN: lucratively 修饰获利的进行方式。

definition_zh: 使安静缓和下来；哄睡；平静的间歇；暂时的平息
definition_en: to make someone feel calm or sleepy, or a short quiet period inside a longer noisy or busy stretch
core_image: 一只手轻轻拍着婴儿的背，哭声一点点弱下去，最后只剩均匀的呼吸
scene: 婴儿刚才还在大哭，妈妈抱起来轻轻摇着。She sang a soft song to lull the baby to sleep.

senses.title: To calm a child into sleep
senses.definition: to make a crying child or animal calm and quiet, especially until it falls asleep
senses.definitionCN: 让哭闹的小孩或动物平静下来，尤其是哄到入睡
senses.example: She lulled the restless baby with a slow, steady song.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一支缓慢而稳定的歌哄那个不安的婴儿入睡。
senses.why: The word was born as a nursery sound, and its first and warmest sense is still a voice or hand calming a small body.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是摇篮边的拟声，它最温暖的第一义项仍然是一道声音或一只手，把小小的身体安抚下来。

senses.title: To ease fears or suspicion
senses.definition: to make people feel less worried, nervous, or suspicious, often for a while only
senses.definitionCN: 使人不那么担心、紧张或怀疑，但往往只是暂时的
senses.example: The manager lulled the fears of the staff with a brief, cheerful talk.
senses.exampleCN: 经理用一段简短而愉快的讲话平息了员工的担忧。
senses.why: The baby and the anxious mind are handled the same way: the volume of alarm is turned down until the feeling falls asleep.
senses.whyCN: 婴儿和焦虑的心被用同样的方式对待：把警报的音量调低，直到那种情绪睡着为止。

senses.title: To deceive into false security
senses.titleCN: 使放松警惕；诱使误以为
senses.definition: to make someone relaxed and careless so that they stop watching for danger
senses.definitionCN: 使人放松、疏忽，从而不再提防危险
senses.example: Several quiet nights had lulled the guards into complacency.
senses.exampleCN: 连着几个平静的夜晚让守卫们变得麻痹大意。
senses.why: The same soothing action is now dangerous: what quiets fear also quiets vigilance, and the word takes a warning tone.
senses.whyCN: 同一种安抚的动作此时变得危险：平息了恐惧，也平息了警觉，于是这个词带上了警告的语调。

senses.title: A quiet spell in a storm
senses.definition: a period during a storm or rough weather when the wind and sea are briefly calm
senses.definitionCN: 风暴或恶劣天气中，风浪短暂平静的一段时间
senses.example: The fishermen put out to sea during a short lull in the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 渔民们趁着风暴中短暂的平静出海。
senses.why: The noun turns the action into a stretch of time: the weather itself is lulled, and the calm has a beginning and an end.
senses.whyCN: 名词用法把动作变成一段时间：天气本身被安抚了，而这份平静有开始也有结束。

senses.title: A pause in activity or talk
senses.definition: a short pause in noise, activity, or conversation when things become quiet
senses.definitionCN: 噪音、活动或交谈中出现的一小段安静停顿
senses.example: There was a lull in the conversation while the waiter poured the wine.
senses.exampleCN: 侍者倒酒时，谈话出现了一段停顿。
senses.why: Any busy stream can stop for a moment, and the word borrows the calm of a sleeping child to describe an ordinary pause.
senses.whyCN: 任何忙碌的流动都可以短暂停一下，这个词借来熟睡孩子般的安静，用来描述一段普通的停顿。

senses.title: A slack period in business
senses.definition: a period when sales, orders, or demand fall quiet between busier phases
senses.definitionCN: 在更繁忙的阶段之间，销量、订单或需求变少的时期
senses.example: December brings a lull in office construction work.
senses.exampleCN: 十二月让办公楼的建设工作进入一个停滞期。
senses.why: The quietness moves from conversation into a market, where the lull is measured in orders rather than in breath.
senses.whyCN: 这种安静从谈话转移到了市场，此时的「平静」用订单而非呼吸来衡量。

senses.title: A brief break in fighting
senses.definition: a temporary stop in bombing, firing, or fighting, often lasting only hours
senses.definitionCN: 轰炸、射击或战斗的暂时停止，通常只持续几个小时
senses.example: Aid trucks crossed the border during the overnight lull.
senses.exampleCN: 援助卡车趁着夜里战斗暂停的时候越过了边境。
senses.why: War has its own breaths, and the noun marks the moment between them, when the noise dies down without the conflict ending.
senses.whyCN: 战争也有自己的呼吸，这个名词标出呼吸之间的那一刻：声音低了下去，冲突却并未结束。

senses.title: To render something quiet or dull
senses.definition: to make a place or mood quiet or dull, so that sound and interest seem to sink
senses.definitionCN: 使某个地方或气氛安静、沉闷下来，声音与兴致都像沉了下去
senses.example: Heavy rain had lulled the whole market into a hush.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨让整个市场沉寂下来，一片安静。
senses.why: When the soothing is applied to a whole place rather than a person, quiet becomes something like heaviness and the mood seems drugged.
senses.whyCN: 当安抚的对象从一个人变成整个地方，安静就近似于沉重，气氛也像是被麻醉了。

intro.en: Lull is an English word of uncertain origin, generally treated as imitative of soft humming and rocking sounds.
intro.cn: lull 是一个来源不确定的英语词，一般认为它模仿了轻声哼唱与摇篮摇晃的声音。

items.en: No Latin or Greek parent is known, so the earliest history is a matter of conjecture.
items.cn: 没有已知的拉丁语或希腊语母词，因此这个词最早的历史只能靠推测。

items.en: It is generally compared with early Scandinavian lulla, the sound used while rocking a child.
items.cn: 一般认为它可以与早期斯堪的纳维亚语的 lulla 相比较，那是摇孩子时发出的声音。

items.en: Lull is treated as an imitative word, a hummed sound that mimics the slow rocking of a cradle.
items.cn: lull 被认为是拟声词，一个模仿摇篮缓摇的哼唱声。

items.en: The verb appears in late Middle English meaning to soothe or rock a child to sleep.
items.cn: 这个动词在中古英语后期出现，意为哄逗或摇晃孩子入睡。

items.en: The verb widens to storms, winds, pain, and the fears of grown people.
items.cn: 动词的用法扩展到风暴、风、疼痛以及成年人的恐惧。

items.en: The noun lull appears later and now names every short calm in wind, talk, trade, or war.
items.cn: 名词形式 lull 出现得更晚，如今用来指风暴、谈话、生意或战争中每一段短暂的平静。

note.en: Lull is a calming word, close to lullaby and to nouns for pauses and quiet periods.
note.cn: lull 是一个「安抚」的词，与 lullaby 以及表示停顿、平静的说法很接近。

normalIntro.en: Lull is a hum: its sound falls softly, and so does the room around it.
normalIntro.cn: lull 就是一声轻哼：它的读音轻轻落下，周围的房间也跟着安静下来。

normal.en: Lull to sleep is the warmest collocation of the verb.
normal.cn: lull to sleep 是这个动词最温暖的搭配。

normal.en: The noun keeps the same shape, so the lull in the conversation is easy to spot.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，所以 the lull in the conversation 很容易认出来。

normal.en: The idiom the lull before the storm warns that calm may not last.
normal.cn: 习语 the lull before the storm 提醒人平静未必能持久。

normal.en: Lullaby is the same humming sound made into a compound noun.
normal.cn: lullaby 就是把同一种轻哼声做成了复合名词。

normal.en: Compare soothe with lull: soothe calms pain, lull brings toward sleep.
normal.cn: 对比 soothe：soothe 偏向止痛，lull 偏向把人带向睡眠。

abstract.cn: 想象一只手轻拍小小的背，哭声慢慢变成呼吸声。

abstract.cn: 想象一个守卫因为夜晚太安静而松懈了警惕。

abstract.en: Picture a pause opening in a noisy market, as if the sound had stepped out.
abstract.cn: 想象喧闹的市场里裂开一段安静，仿佛声音自己走出去了一会儿。

examples.en: The soft rain lulled us to sleep.
examples.cn: 轻柔的雨声哄我们睡着了。

examples.en: Prices rose sharply after a long lull in the housing market.
examples.cn: 房地产市场长期停滞之后，房价急剧上涨。

examples.en: Do not let the quiet lull you into a false sense of security.
examples.cn: 不要让这份安静哄得你产生虚假的安全感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉」——母亲轻轻拉上摇篮的帘子，孩子就安静下来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源不确定，一般认为源自模仿摇篮哼唱与轻摇之声的拟声用法，可与早期斯堪的纳维亚语 lulla 相比较。

sensesIntro.en: Lull starts with a voice calming a child, turns the same soothing on fear, makes the calm look like deception, and finally becomes the noun for every short quiet in weather, talk, trade, or war.
sensesIntro.cn: lull 从安抚孩子的嗓音开始，把同样的安抚转向恐惧，让这份平静带上欺骗的意味，最后变成名词，指天气、谈话、生意或战争中每一段短暂的安静。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand patting a baby to sleep while the crying fades into steady breathing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手拍着婴儿入睡，哭声渐渐变成均匀的呼吸。

branches.en: CHILD: the oldest and warmest sense, a voice bringing a small body to sleep.
branches.cn: 孩子线：最古老也最温暖的义项，一道嗓音把小小的身体带入睡意。

branches.en: MIND: fear and suspicion are treated as a crying that can be quieted.
branches.cn: 心绪线：恐惧与怀疑被当作一阵可以被哄住的哭声。

branches.en: TRAP: the same soothing action lets danger in, because it also silences vigilance.
branches.cn: 陷阱线：同一个安抚动作也放进了危险，因为它同时让警觉沉默。

branches.en: PAUSES: storm, talk, trade, and war all have their short breathing spaces.
branches.cn: 停顿线：风暴、谈话、生意与战争都有自己的短促喘息。

branches.en: MOOD: applied to a whole place, the calm becomes a heavy quiet that seems to spread over everything.
branches.cn: 气氛线：当它用于整个地方，平静就变成一种沉沉的安静，仿佛笼罩一切。

intro.en: Lull is a short Germanic word, so its word building is thin: the family is lull, lulled, lulling, and the compound lullaby.
intro.cn: lull 是一个简短的日耳曼语词，构词层次很薄：词族只有 lull、lulled、lulling 以及复合词 lullaby。

latinIntro.en: Lull has no Latin ancestor, and its origin is uncertain; the related English forms are all built on the root lull itself.
latinIntro.cn: lull 没有拉丁语祖词，来源不确定；相关的英语形式都由 lull 这个词根本身构成。

items.example: Lull is the root of the whole small family.
items.exampleCN: lull 是整个小词族的词根。

items.example: The suffix -ing gives lulling.

items.example: Lulling describes a sleepy, rocking sound.
items.exampleCN: lulling 描述一种令人困倦的摇晃声。

items.example: The suffix -s gives lulls in both uses.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 同时构成动词与名词形式。

items.example: Lulls names several short calms in a row.
items.exampleCN: lulls 指接连出现的几段短暂平静。

items.example: The pattern lull into carries the trap sense.
items.exampleCN: lull into 这一搭配承载陷阱义。

senses.title: A gentle song to send a child to sleep
senses.definition: a quiet, repeated song sung softly to a baby or young child to soothe it and help it sleep
senses.definitionCN: 轻声反复唱给婴儿或幼儿听、使其安静入睡的歌曲
senses.example: Every night her grandmother sang the same lullaby at bedtime.
senses.exampleCN: 每天晚上睡前，她奶奶都会唱同一首摇篮曲。
senses.why: The word has two halves: lull means to calm and quieten, and the second part is an old word for a song, so a lullaby is literally a calming song.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由两半组成：lull 意为「使安静」，后半是表示「歌」的古词，所以摇篮曲字面上就是「使安静的歌曲」。

senses.title: A melody that soothes adults too
senses.definition: a melody or piece of music that has the same slow, soothing quality as a children song, often felt to calm adults
senses.definitionCN: 具有与童谣相同舒缓、安抚特质的旋律或乐曲，常被认为能抚慰成年人
senses.example: When the concert ended, the band played a slow lullaby to calm the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 演出结束时，乐队奏了一首舒缓的摇篮曲似的曲子，让人群安静下来。
senses.why: The lulling effect is what makes the song; once listeners hear that, they can apply the word to any music that gently slows the pulse.
senses.whyCN: 起安眠作用的是那种「哄」的效果；听者一旦抓住这种感觉，就会用它来形容任何让心跳慢下来的轻柔音乐。

senses.title: Familiar phrases that never change
senses.titleCN: 千篇一律的套话；陈词滥调
senses.definition: a few comforting, repeated phrases or statements that are meant to calm people rather than to inform them
senses.definitionCN: 几句令人安心的、反复使用的短语或说法，目的只是安抚而不是提供信息
senses.example: The minister offered a lullaby of promises but no clear plan.
senses.exampleCN: 部长给出一连串安抚性的承诺，却没有明确的计划。
senses.why: Because a lullaby is exactly that, a familiar refrain, the word is borrowed to describe slogans that send listeners to sleep instead of making them think.
senses.whyCN: 因为摇篮曲正是熟悉重复的调子，这个词便被借来形容那些让人昏昏欲睡、而不是促人思考的口号。

intro.en: Lullaby joins lull, to calm someone to sleep, and an old second element meaning a song, related to bye-bye and to the refrain lulla.
intro.cn: lullaby 由 lull（哄人入睡）与表示「歌」的古老成分组成，后者与 bye-bye 以及反复出现的「lulla」唱词相关。

items.en: Lollen means to sing softly or soothe, probably an echoic word.
items.cn: 中古英语 lollen 意为轻声歌唱或哄孩子，一般认为属拟声词。

items.en: Lull enters English meaning to calm or quieten someone.
items.cn: lull 进入英语，意为使安静、使人镇静。

items.en: Lullaby is formed from lull plus an old song word, so it means a soothing song.
items.cn: lullaby 由 lull 加古老表示「歌」的成分构成，意为安抚性的歌曲。

items.en: The second element is linked to Scottish and dialect words meaning to sing, and to the refrain lulla and the phrase bye-bye.
items.cn: 后半成分一般与苏格兰语及方言中表示「唱歌」的词、以及唱词 lulla 和短语 bye-bye 相联系。

items.en: The word spreads to any soothing melody and to figurative phrases that calm listeners.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到任何安抚性的旋律，也用于比喻那些让人安心的套话。

note.en: Lullaby is a compound whose first part is lull; its look-alikes are members of that calming family, and its near meanings are other songs and sounds that soothe.
note.cn: lullaby 是复合词，前半部分就是 lull；形近词属于「使安静」这个词族，近义词是其他起安抚作用的歌和声音。

normalIntro.en: Lullaby is built from lull, a word that means to quieten someone, plus an old song word.
normalIntro.cn: lullaby 由 lull 构成，lull 意为「使某人安静」，再加上一个古老的「歌」字。

normal.en: Lull means to calm someone gently, and the rest of the word adds song.
normal.cn: lull 指温柔地使人安静，后面的部分再加上「歌」，就是哄睡的歌。

normal.en: The plural is lullabies: a consonant plus y changes to ies.
normal.cn: 复数是 lullabies：辅音字母加 y 结尾，要把 y 变成 ies。

normal.en: You sing or hum a lullaby, and you sing it to a baby.
normal.cn: 搭配是 sing 或 hum a lullaby，而且是对婴儿唱。

normal.en: Lullabying is rare as a verb; the noun is what you will mostly meet.
normal.cn: lullaby 作动词很罕见，你遇到的多半是名词。

normal.en: Compare cradle song: it means the same, but lullaby also carries the feeling of calming and sleep.
normal.cn: 对比 cradle song：两者意思相同，但 lullaby 多了「安抚、入睡」的感觉。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd nodding as one soothing phrase is repeated again and again.

examples.en: She sang a lullaby to put the restless baby back to sleep.

examples.en: Many lullabies are passed down through generations without any written notes.
examples.cn: 许多摇篮曲没有乐谱，靠一代代口耳相传。

examples.en: The singer closed the show with a quiet melody that felt like a lullaby.
examples.cn: 歌手用一段安静的、像摇篮曲一样的旋律结束了演出。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉了白」——拉了拉被子，孩子就睡着了，轻轻哼的就是摇篮曲；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语 lollen（轻声唱、哄孩子，一般认为属拟声词）→ lull（使安静）＋古老表示「歌」的成分（与苏格兰语及方言中「唱歌」的词、唱词 lulla、短语 bye-bye 有关，具体来源不确定）→ 英语 lullaby，核心义「使人安静下来的歌」。

sensesIntro.en: Lullaby begins as a song that lulls a child to sleep, then widens to any soothing melody, and finally works figuratively for comforting phrases.
sensesIntro.cn: lullaby 先指哄孩子入睡的歌，再扩展到任何有安抚作用的旋律，最后比喻地用于那些只是安抚人的套话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mother rocking a sleepy child and humming softly.
core.cn: 核心意象：母亲抱着困倦的孩子轻轻摇晃、低声哼唱。

branches.en: A song to send a child to sleep is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 哄孩子入睡的歌是字面义项。

branches.en: Any melody with the same soothing quality borrows the word.
branches.cn: 任何具有同样安抚效果的旋律都会借用这个词。

branches.en: Repeated comforting phrases are the figurative extension.
branches.cn: 反复出现的安抚性套话是比喻扩展。

branches.en: Both a cradle song and a soothing concert piece slow the pulse of the listener.
branches.cn: 摇篮曲与安抚性的演奏曲都会让听者的心跳慢下来。

branches.en: A lullaby and a lullaby of promises share the aim of sending someone to sleep.
branches.cn: 摇篮曲与安抚性承诺的共同点，都是想让人「睡着」。

intro.en: Lullaby is a compound, not an affix word: lull supplies the calming action and the old song element completes the name.
intro.cn: lullaby 是复合词而非词缀词：lull 提供「使安静」的动作，古老的「歌」字补全名称。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved; the word grew inside English from a medieval singing word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词不涉及拉丁语成分，它是在英语内部由中古英语的「唱歌」词演化而来。

items.example: Lollen is the probable ancestor of lull.
items.exampleCN: lollen 很可能是 lull 的前身。

items.meaning: to calm someone gently to sleep
items.example: Lull is the first half of lullaby.
items.exampleCN: lull 是 lullaby 的前半部分。

items.meaning: a gentle song to send a child to sleep
items.example: Lullaby is the full compound.
items.exampleCN: lullaby 是完整的复合词。

items.meaning: plural of nouns ending in consonant plus y
items.meaningCN: 辅音加 y 结尾名词的复数词尾
items.example: The ending -ies gives lullabies.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ies 构成 lullabies。

items.example: Lullabies is the standard plural.
items.exampleCN: lullabies 是标准复数形式。

items.example: Lulling builds on lull with the suffix -ing.
items.exampleCN: lulling 由 lull 加后缀 -ing 构成。

items.example: Lullingly adds the adverb ending -ly.
items.exampleCN: lullingly 加了副词词尾 -ly。

items.example: Lullabying shows the rare verb use of the word.
items.exampleCN: lullabying 展示了这个词罕见的动词用法。

items.meaning: a lullaby, especially an instrumental one
items.example: Berceuse enters English from French as a musical term.
items.exampleCN: berceuse 是从法语借入的音乐术语。

derivatives.zh: lullaby 的前半部分，同源单用，义为「使安静；哄睡」
lull 加 -ing，义为「催人入睡的；舒缓的」
法语借词，指摇篮曲，尤指器乐作品

definition_zh: 潜伏；潜藏；暗藏；隐藏着；埋伏等待；徘徊
definition_en: to wait in a hidden place, usually with a harmful purpose, or to exist unseen and ready to appear
core_image: 一只猫缩在灌木后面，只露出眼睛，等猎物走近才扑出
scene: 网络广告里一个未经验证的链接悄悄藏着风险，等着有人点击。Scammers lurk on social media waiting for people to reply.
sceneCN: 这里 lurk 是「潜伏；暗藏」（第 1 个义项：躲起来等待机会，常带不良目的）；句意：骗子潜伏在社交媒体上，等着有人回复。

pos.zh: 潜藏处（海面礁石间的暗藏之处）

derivatives.zh: 由动词 lurk 加施动后缀 -er 构成，指潜藏的人（也指只在网上看帖、不发言的人）
lurk 加 -ing，指「潜伏状态」，也可作形容词「潜伏的、暗藏的」

senses.title: To wait hidden for a chance to harm
senses.definition: to stay in a hidden place, especially waiting to attack or do something wrong
senses.definitionCN: 躲藏在隐蔽的地方，尤指等待袭击或做不好的事
senses.example: Someone was lurking behind the fence, watching the house.
senses.exampleCN: 有人躲在篱笆后面，盯着那栋房子。
senses.why: The word first describes an animal pulling itself out of sight before it catches its prey, and that crouching, motionless waiting is the core image.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初描写动物在捕捉猎物前缩起身子藏起来，那种蹲伏不动的等待就是核心意象。

senses.title: To exist unseen and ready to appear
senses.definition: used of a danger, feeling, or problem that is present but not obvious until it shows itself
senses.definitionCN: 指危险、情绪或问题已存在却不明显，直到突然显现
senses.example: Danger can lurk in the most ordinary of places.
senses.exampleCN: 危险可能暗藏在最普通的地方。
senses.why: Because lurk means to be there without being seen, abstract things can lurk too, as long as they stay out of sight until the right moment.
senses.whyCN: 因为 lurk 指「在而不显」，抽象之物只要藏到某个时刻才现身，也可以用 lurk。

senses.title: To read online without speaking
senses.definition: to read messages or posts in an online group without adding anything yourself
senses.definitionCN: 在线上群组里只看消息或帖子，自己不发任何内容
senses.example: Most members lurk in the chat and never post a reply.
senses.exampleCN: 大部分成员在群里潜水，从不回复。
senses.why: The hiding-while-watching image fits an online reader who stays quietly in the background, so internet culture borrowed the word.
senses.whyCN: 「躲着看」的画面正好契合安静待在背景里的网上读者，网络文化便借用了这个词。

senses.title: An old word for moving slowly and furtively
senses.definition: in older use, to move about in a slow, secretive way, keeping out of sight
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法中指鬼鬼祟祟、缓慢地走动、避开视线
senses.example: In old novels, suspicious figures lurk through the streets after dark.
senses.exampleCN: 在老小说里，可疑人物常在入夜后潜行于街头。
senses.why: Before it settled on waiting, the verb could name secret motion, and this older shade survives in literary writing.
senses.whyCN: 在固定为「等待」之前，这个词也能表示秘密的移动，这一层旧色彩保留在文学写作里。

senses.title: The place where something hidden waits
senses.definition: a hidden spot where a person or creature waits or rests out of sight
senses.definitionCN: 人或生物躲藏、等待时所在的隐蔽之处
senses.example: Fishing boats keep well away from the lurk among the rocks.
senses.exampleCN: 渔船都远远避开礁石间那一处暗藏处。
senses.why: It is a short step from the action to the place: once lurk means to stay hidden, its name can mark the hiding place itself.
senses.whyCN: 从动作到地点只有一步之遥：既然 lurk 表示躲藏，它的名词形式就可以指躲藏的地方。

intro.en: Lurk is probably a Scandinavian loanword in Middle English, first written lurkyn, and it has no reliable Latin or Greek ancestor.
intro.cn: lurk 一般认为是在中古英语时期借自斯堪的纳维亚语，最早写作 lurkyn，没有可靠的拉丁语或希腊语祖词。

items.en: The form is likely continental, related to Dutch loeren and German lauern, meaning to lie in wait.
items.cn: 其形式很可能来自大陆，与荷兰语 loeren、德语 lauern（埋伏等待）同源。

items.en: Evidence of a borrowed Norse ancestor is thin, so most handbooks leave the exact source uncertain.
items.cn: 来自古诺斯语的直接证据不多，所以多数辞书把确切来源标为不确定。

items.en: Lurkyn is recorded in the fourteenth century for hiding and for lying in wait.
items.cn: 中古英语 lurkyn 在十四世纪已有记载，义为躲藏和埋伏等待。

items.en: The verb grows a noun for a hiding place at sea, still used in nautical use.
items.cn: 动词衍生出指海上躲藏之处的名词，至今保留在航海用语中。

items.en: Literary writers extend the verb to dangers and feelings that are present but unseen.
items.cn: 十九世纪的文学写作把这个词扩展到潜伏着却看不见的危险与情绪。

items.en: Internet use gives a new sense, reading messages silently in an online group.
items.cn: 网络时代产生新义：在线上群组里只看消息不发言。

note.en: Lurk sits in a family with lurker, lurking, and lurch; its near meanings are other verbs for waiting secretly and hiding.
note.cn: lurk 与 lurker、lurking、lurch 构成一个词族；它的近义词是其他表示「暗中等待、躲藏」的动词。

entries.definition: a person who stays hidden or who reads but never posts
entries.definitionCN: 潜伏者；网络上的潜水者

entries.definition: the state of hiding or waiting out of sight
entries.definitionCN: 潜伏；潜伏的

entries.definition: to move suddenly and unsteadily
entries.definitionCN: 突然踉跄；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to move or wait quietly so as not to be noticed
entries.definitionCN: 鬼祟地躲藏；潜行

entries.definition: to move about quietly while hunting
entries.definitionCN: （猎物）悄悄徘徊觅食

entries.definition: to follow or approach prey stealthily
entries.definitionCN: 悄悄跟踪；潜近猎物

normalIntro.en: Lurk is a short verb with a soft sound, and its family grows through -er and -ing.
normalIntro.cn: lurk 是发音轻柔的短动词，词族通过 -er 与 -ing 扩展。

normal.en: Lurk goes with the preposition in or behind, as in lurk in the shadows.
normal.cn: lurk 常接 in 或 behind，如 lurk in the shadows 潜伏在暗处。

normal.en: Add -er and lurk becomes a person: a lurker.
normal.cn: 加 -er 就把 lurk 变成人：lurker 潜水者。

normal.en: Add -ing for the state: the lurking danger.
normal.cn: 加 -ing 表示状态：the lurking danger 潜藏的危险。

normal.en: Do not confuse lurk with lurch, which means to sway or stagger.
normal.cn: 别把 lurk 和 lurch 弄混，lurch 是「趔趄、摇晃」。

normal.en: Compare skulk: skulk stresses moving secretly, lurk stresses staying still and hidden.
normal.cn: 对比 skulk：skulk 强调偷偷移动，lurk 强调静止躲藏。

abstract.en: Picture a cat pressed flat behind a low fence, only its eyes moving.
abstract.cn: 想象一只猫趴在低矮的篱笆后，只有眼睛在动。

abstract.en: Picture a calm pond with something dark waiting just under the surface.
abstract.cn: 想象平静的池塘，水面下有个黑影静静等着。

abstract.en: Picture a quiet reader who watched a message thread but never typed a word.
abstract.cn: 想象一个安静的人刷完了整个帖子，却始终一个字都没发。

examples.en: Dark shapes lurked at the edge of the forest.
examples.cn: 森林边缘潜藏着一些黑色的身影。

examples.en: The article warns that hidden fees lurk in many cheap deals.
examples.cn: 文章提醒，许多廉价交易里暗藏着隐性费用。

examples.en: Two men were seen lurking near the back door of the shop.
examples.cn: 有人看见两个男人在商店后门附近徘徊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「乐克」——躲在角落里的乐克，悄悄看着你不敢出声；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为中古英语借自斯堪的纳维亚语（古诺斯语来源证据不足，标为不确定），与荷兰语 loeren、德语 lauern（埋伏等待）同源；中古英语 lurkyn → 英语 lurk，核心义「躲着不出声地等待」。

sensesIntro.en: Lurk starts with an animal waiting out of sight, widens to unseen dangers, then to people watching quietly online, and finally to the hidden place itself.
sensesIntro.cn: lurk 先指动物隐身等待，再扩展到看不见的危险，又扩展到网上默默围观的人，最后指躲藏的地点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hunched figure in the bushes, still and watchful.
core.cn: 核心意象：灌木丛后蜷着身子、一动不动紧盯前方的人。

branches.en: Waiting hidden to do harm is the central sense.
branches.cn: 隐身等待、伺机行动是中心义项。

branches.en: Unseen dangers inherit the hiding part of the image.
branches.cn: 看不见的危险继承了意象中「隐藏」的一面。

branches.en: Online silent reading is the newest extension.
branches.cn: 网上只看不说是最新的扩展义项。

branches.en: Older secret movement and the hiding place itself are the edges of the family.
branches.cn: 较旧的秘密移动与躲藏地点是这个词族的边缘义项。

branches.en: Both a waiting person and a hidden danger keep still until the moment comes.
branches.cn: 潜伏者与暗藏的危险都会一直不动，直到时机到来。

intro.en: Lurk is a Germanic word with no Latin root; its family is built in English with -er and -ing.
intro.cn: lurk 是日耳曼语源的词，没有拉丁词根；它的词族是在英语中用 -er 和 -ing 构成的。

latinIntro.en: Latin plays no part here; early forms such as lurkyn came from Middle English borrowing, not from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语在这里没有地位；lurkyn 这样的早期形式来自中古英语的借用，而非拉丁语。

items.example: Lurkyn is the earliest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: lurkyn 是最早有记录的形式。

items.example: Lurk loses its final syllable in modern spelling.
items.exampleCN: 现代拼写去掉了末尾的音节。

items.example: The suffix -er forms lurker.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 lurker。

items.meaning: a person who hides or watches silently
items.example: Lurker is common in online communities.
items.exampleCN: lurker 在网络社区中很常见。

items.meaning: the act or state of doing something
items.example: The suffix -ing forms lurking.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 lurking。

items.meaning: hiding, or the state of hiding
items.example: Lurking can describe a hidden danger.
items.exampleCN: lurking 可以形容暗藏的危险。

items.exampleCN: lauern 是相近的日耳曼语同源词。

items.example: Loeren shows the same continental shape.

items.exampleCN: lurch 是拼写相近但来源不同的词。
