lurk 加 -ing，指潜伏的状态或「暗藏的」

definition_zh: 强壮的；健壮的；精力充沛的；粗壮有力的；健硕的
definition_en: strong, healthy, and full of energy, often used of a person or of a loud or vigorous voice or action
core_image: 一个红着脸、声音洪亮、扛着重物仍然脚步轻快的人
scene: 清晨的山坡上，牧羊人扯开嗓子吆喝，还抬起自家的小羊羔展示给路人看。The shepherd raised a lusty cheer as the lambs ran across the hill.
sceneCN: 这里 lusty 是「洪亮的、有力的」（第 2 个义项：声音或动作粗壮有力）；句意：羊羔跑过山坡时，牧羊人发出了一声洪亮的欢呼。

pos.zh: 强壮的；健壮的；精力充沛的

derivatives.zh: lusty 加 -ness 构成，义为「强健；精力充沛」
lusty 把 y 变 i 再加 -ly，义为「响亮地；有力地；健壮地」
与 lusty 同源的基础名词，原指强烈欲望或乐趣，现代主要指色欲，正是 lur 词根「欢乐」的偏移

senses.title: Strong, healthy and full of vigour
senses.definition: having strong, healthy body and plenty of energy, especially when this is obvious to others
senses.definitionCN: 身体强壮健康、精力旺盛，尤其是一眼就能看出来
senses.example: The lusty young farmer carried the whole sack on one shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 那个健壮的小伙子用一只肩膀就扛起了整袋粮食。
senses.why: Lusty goes back to a word for pleasure and lively health, so someone in that state is pictured as glowing with physical vigour.
senses.whyCN: lusty 源于表示「欢乐、旺盛的健康」的词，所以处于这种状态的人被画成浑身透着活力。

senses.title: Loud and vigorous in sound or action
senses.definition: used of a voice, shout, or action that is strong and full, as if powered by a healthy body
senses.definitionCN: 指嗓音、呼喊或动作饱满有力，仿佛由健壮的身体驱动
senses.example: The crowd gave a lusty cheer when the team scored.
senses.exampleCN: 球队得分时，人群发出洪亮的欢呼。
senses.why: Vigour is not only in muscles; a strong body produces a full voice, so the word shifts to sounds and deeds that have the same hearty quality.
senses.whyCN: 活力不只在肌肉里；强壮的身体也发出饱满的声音，于是这个词转到同样「有底气」的声音与动作上。

senses.title: Vigorous healthy growth, said of plants
senses.definition: used of plants or parts of them that grow strongly and abundantly
senses.definitionCN: 指植物或植株部分生长强劲、繁茂
senses.example: The garden was full of lusty green shoots after the spring rain.
senses.exampleCN: 春雨过后，园子里满是茁壮的绿芽。
senses.why: What is healthy and abundant in a person can be applied to what grows thick and fast in a garden.
senses.whyCN: 在人身上表示健康丰沛的词，也能用来形容园中长得又密又快的东西。

senses.title: Archaic use for cheerful and exuberant
senses.definition: in old literature, in good spirits, hearty and cheerfully lively
senses.definitionCN: 在旧文学中表示心情好、热情爽朗、兴高采烈
senses.example: The folk songs keep the lusty spirit of the harvest feast alive.
senses.exampleCN: 这些民歌让丰收宴会上那种爽朗的欢乐气氛延续至今。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is delight, so readings of older texts still carry the note of hearty cheerfulness.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早的一层意义就是「喜悦」，所以读旧文本时仍带着爽朗快活的味道。

intro.en: Lusty is formed in Middle English from lust, which once meant pleasure and eager health rather than sexual desire.
intro.cn: lusty 在中古英语里由 lust 加后缀构成，而 lust 原指喜悦和旺盛的健康，并非现在常说的色欲。

items.en: Lust means pleasure, delight, or inclination in Old English.
items.cn: 古英语 lust 意为喜悦、乐趣或意愿。

items.en: Lusty is built from lust on the pattern of other adjectives ending in -y.
items.cn: 中古英语按其他 -y 结尾形容词的模式由 lust 构造出 lusty。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in the sense of cheerful, merry, and healthy.
items.cn: 形容词在十四世纪有记载，义为欢乐、愉快、健康的。

items.en: Lusty comes to describe strong bodies and full voices, while the noun lust narrows to sexual desire.
items.cn: 现代英语中 lusty 转向形容强壮的身体和饱满的声音，而名词 lust 收窄为色欲。

items.en: The adjective is now often literary, set beside strong, hearty, and vigorous.
items.cn: 这个形容词今天偏文学色彩，常与 strong、hearty、vigorous 并列。

note.en: Lusty is the adjective of the lust family; its look-alikes are closely related forms, and its near meanings are adjectives for strength and vigour.
note.cn: lusty 是 lust 词族的形容词；形近词是同族近亲，近义词是表示强壮和精力充沛的其他形容词。

entries.definition: with strength and spirit
entries.definitionCN: 有力地；响亮地

entries.definition: the quality of being strong and energetic
entries.definitionCN: 强健；精力充沛

entries.definition: strong sexual desire, or formerly any great pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的性欲，旧义为强烈喜悦

entries.definition: full of energy and strength
entries.definitionCN: 精力旺盛的；有力的

entries.definition: strong and healthy, able to stand hard conditions
entries.definitionCN: 强健的；结实耐用的

entries.definition: warm, cheerful, and full of life
entries.definitionCN: 热情爽朗的；丰盛的

normalIntro.en: Lusty is lust plus -y, and its family runs through lustiness and lustily.
normalIntro.cn: lusty 是 lust 加 -y 构成的形容词，词族有 lustiness 与 lustily。

normal.en: Lusty used to mean merry and healthy, much wider than lust today.
normal.cn: lusty 旧义是「愉快、健康」，比今天的 lust 含义宽得多。

normal.en: The noun is lustiness and the adverb is lustily.
normal.cn: 名词是 lustiness，副词是 lustily。

normal.en: The comparatives are lustier and lustiest: y becomes i before -er.
normal.cn: 比较级是 lustier、最高级是 lustiest：加 -er 时 y 要变 i。

normal.en: Lusty is usually used of people, voices, and appetites, and rarely of objects.
normal.cn: lusty 多修饰人、嗓音和食欲，很少修饰物件。

normal.en: Compare hearty: hearty stresses warmth, lusty stresses raw strength.
normal.cn: 对比 hearty：hearty 强调热情，lusty 强调粗壮的力量。

abstract.en: Picture a farmer lifting a full sack and laughing out loud.
abstract.cn: 想象一个农夫提起满满一袋粮食，还放声大笑。

abstract.en: Picture a stadium where one deep shout rises above the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象体育场里有一声浑厚的呐喊盖过了其他声音。

abstract.en: Picture young shoots pushing through soil after rain, thick and quick.
abstract.cn: 想象雨后的嫩芽又粗又快地从土里顶出来。

examples.en: The lusty crowd joined the chorus without any prompting.
examples.cn: 人群热情高涨，不用任何人带就跟着唱起了合唱。

examples.en: He took a lusty bite of bread after the long walk.
examples.cn: 走了很长一段路后，他大口咬下了一大块面包。

examples.en: Her lusty laugh could be heard across the whole hall.
examples.cn: 她那爽朗的笑声整个大厅都听得见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉斯蒂」——拉起斯蒂的名字，是因为他一口气能拉起重物，力气大得很；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 lust（喜悦、乐趣、意愿）→ 中古英语 lusty（欢乐的、健康的）→ 英语 lusty，核心义「健康充沛的活力」；同族名词 lust 后来收窄为色欲。

sensesIntro.en: Lusty first names the health and vigour of a body, then the fullness of a voice or action, then strong growth in plants, and in old texts hearty cheerfulness.
sensesIntro.cn: lusty 先指身体的健康与活力，再指声音、动作的饱满有力，然后指植物茁壮生长，而在旧文本中指爽朗的欢乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red-faced person lifting a heavy load and laughing loudly.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人红着脸扛起重物，还大声笑着。

branches.en: Bodily strength and energy is the central sense.
branches.cn: 身体的强壮与精力是中心义项。

branches.en: Full, hearty sound is the energy made audible.
branches.cn: 饱满洪亮的声音是活力的听觉表现。

branches.en: Vigorous growth transfers the image to plants.
branches.cn: 茁壮的生长把这一意象转给植物。

branches.en: Old cheerful use keeps the original note of delight.
branches.cn: 旧义的「欢乐」保留了最初的愉悦色彩。

branches.en: A strong body, a loud voice and a thick shoot all show the same overflowing health.
branches.cn: 强壮的身体、洪亮的嗓音与粗壮的嫩芽，展现的都是同一种溢出的健康。

intro.en: Lusty is a native English formation of lust plus -y, with the family lustiness and lustily.
intro.cn: lusty 是英语本土构词：lust 加 -y，词族有 lustiness 与 lustily。

latinIntro.en: Lusty has no Latin root; its base lust is a Germanic word that has stayed inside English.
latinIntro.cn: lusty 没有拉丁词根；基础词 lust 是日耳曼语词，一直留在英语内部。

items.example: Lust begins as a word for pleasure.
items.exampleCN: lust 起初是表示喜悦的词。

items.example: Lusty keeps the healthy side of lust.
items.exampleCN: lusty 保留了 lust 中「健康」的一面。

items.example: The suffix -y builds lusty from lust.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 由 lust 构成 lusty。

items.example: Lustiness adds the noun ending -ness.
items.exampleCN: lustiness 加了名词词尾 -ness。

items.example: Lustily shows y changing to i before -ly.
items.exampleCN: lustily 显示了 y 在 -ly 前变为 i。

items.example: Lustier is the regular comparative.
items.exampleCN: lustier 是规则的比较级。

items.example: Lustiest is the regular superlative.
items.exampleCN: lustiest 是规则的最高级。

items.example: Hearty is the nearest everyday synonym.
items.exampleCN: hearty 是最接近的日常近义词。

derivatives.zh: lusty 加 -ness，指强健与精力充沛
lusty 变 y 为 i 加 -ly，指响亮地、有力地
lusty 的词根名词，旧义为强烈喜悦，今多指色欲

definition_zh: 茂盛的；繁茂的；浓密的；华丽的；繁复的
definition_en: growing thickly and strongly, or rich and elaborate in appearance
core_image: 一片枝条疯长、叶子密得看不见天光的林间草地
scene: 雨后的山坡上，草叶和野花一起向上蹿，密得盖住了小路。After the rain, the hillside was covered by luxuriant grass and wild flowers.
sceneCN: 这里 luxuriant 是「茂盛、繁茂」（第 1 个义项：植物长得又密又壮）；句意：雨后，山坡被茂盛的草和野花覆盖。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀构成，指茂盛、繁茂的状态
由形容词加副词后缀构成，指茂盛地、繁复地
同源名词，原义为过度的繁盛，今指奢侈、奢侈品
同源动词，指尽情享受、恣意生长

senses.title: Growing thickly and strongly
senses.definition: describing plants that grow in abundance, with many strong stems and leaves
senses.definitionCN: 形容植物长得又多又壮、枝叶密集成片
senses.example: Luxuriant shrubs blocked the view of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 茂密的灌木挡住了看河的视线。
senses.why: The Latin verb luxuriari means to grow too vigorously, so luxuriant keeps that image of abundance beyond restraint.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「疯长、长过头」，luxuriant 保留的正是这种不受节制的丰盛画面。

senses.title: Thick and full of hair or foliage
senses.definition: describing hair, beard, or vegetation that is dense and full
senses.definitionCN: 形容头发、胡须或枝叶厚实而繁密
senses.example: The old man had a luxuriant white beard.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老人留着浓密的白胡子。
senses.why: If grass can grow too thickly, then anything growing densely can be called luxuriant by the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 既然草可以长得密到失控，那么任何密集生长之物都能用同一幅画面来形容。

senses.title: Rich and elaborate in style
senses.definition: describing language, design, or decoration that is rich, ornate, and full of detail
senses.definitionCN: 形容语言、设计或装饰富丽、繁复、细节丰富
senses.example: The palace was filled with luxuriant carvings and gold paint.
senses.exampleCN: 宫殿里到处是华丽的雕饰和描金。
senses.why: Overgrowth of plants became a metaphor for overgrowth of ornament, so luxuriant also describes abundant decoration.
senses.whyCN: 植物的过度生长被借来形容装饰的过度丰富，于是 luxuriant 也能表示繁复的装饰。

senses.title: Abundant in imagination or feeling
senses.definition: describing thought or feeling that pours out in abundance
senses.definitionCN: 形容思绪或情感充沛而源源不断地涌出
senses.example: The poet was known for her luxuriant imagination.
senses.exampleCN: 这位诗人以丰富的想象力著称。
senses.why: The sense of physical abundance extends to inner life, where ideas and feelings can also grow luxuriantly.
senses.whyCN: 物质上的丰盛可以延伸到内心世界，想法与情感同样能够「疯长」。

senses.title: Flourishing or prosperous
senses.definition: describing a place or period that is thriving and full of life
senses.definitionCN: 形容地方或时期生机旺盛、欣欣向荣
senses.example: The market grew into a luxuriant trading town.
senses.exampleCN: 这个集市渐渐发展成一座繁荣的贸易小镇。
senses.why: A place where growth cannot be held back looks like a garden run wild, so luxuriant can describe prosperity.
senses.whyCN: 一个生长势头压不住的地方就像疯长的花园，所以 luxuriant 也能形容繁荣。

senses.title: Deep and full in colour or sound
senses.definition: describing a colour voice or tone that is rich and full
senses.definitionCN: 形容颜色或声音浓重、饱满
senses.example: The garden was full of luxuriant green and birdsong.
senses.exampleCN: 花园里满是浓郁的绿色和鸟鸣。
senses.why: The idea of fullness carries over from sight to colour and hearing, where richness is felt as depth.
senses.whyCN: 「满」的感觉从视觉转移到颜色和听觉上，丰盈便表现为浓重与深沉。

senses.title: Overgrown and excessive
senses.definition: describing growth or style that has gone too far and needs cutting back
senses.definitionCN: 形容生长或文风过度繁盛、需要修剪
senses.example: The garden had turned into luxuriant weeds.
senses.exampleCN: 花园已经变成了长得过盛的杂草。
senses.why: The root verb already contains the idea of too much, so a critical, slightly negative edge sits inside the word.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的拉丁词根本身就含有「过头」之意，因此字里带有一点批判、略嫌过度的色彩。

intro.en: Luxuriant goes back to Latin luxuriosus, given to excess, from luxus, meaning abundance or excess.
intro.cn: luxuriant 可上溯到拉丁语 luxuriosus（放纵的、过分的），源于 luxus（丰盛、过度）。

items.en: Luxus means excess or extravagance, and luxuria means profuse growth or rankness.
items.cn: luxus 意为过度、奢侈；luxuria 指繁茂、疯长。

items.en: The verb luxuriari means to grow rank, to shoot up, and also to revel.
items.cn: 动词 luxuriari 意为疯长、茁壮生长，也有纵情享乐之意。

items.en: The adjective luxuriosus describes someone given to excess.
items.cn: 形容词 luxuriosus 形容放纵、过分之人。

items.en: Late Latin luxurians develops the botanical sense of growing abundant and thick.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 luxurians 发展出植物长得繁密茂盛的用法。

items.en: Luxuriant enters English in the sixteenth century, first of plants and then of style.
items.cn: 十六世纪 luxuriant 进入英语，先用于植物，再用于文风与装饰。

items.en: Luxuriant and luxury split apart, with luxuriant keeping the sense of abundant growth.
items.cn: 现代英语中 luxuriant 与 luxury 分工明确，前者保留「丰盛生长」之意。

note.en: Luxuriant is the adjective of overflowing growth, close to luxuriance and luxury, and to other growth words such as lush and verdant.
note.cn: luxuriant 是表示「过盛生长」的形容词，与 luxuriance、luxury 同族，也与 lush、verdant 等生长词相邻。

entries.definition: very comfortable and expensive
entries.definitionCN: 豪华的；奢侈的，与 luxuriant 同出拉丁词根，但形容舒适奢华而非生长

entries.definition: the state of growing abundantly
entries.definitionCN: 茂盛；繁茂

entries.definition: great comfort or expensive things
entries.definitionCN: 奢侈；奢侈品，与原词共享「过盛」的词根

entries.definition: growing thickly and healthily
entries.definitionCN: 茂盛的；繁茂的

entries.definition: covered with green grass or plants
entries.definitionCN: 青翠的；翠绿的

entries.definition: developing well and becoming successful
entries.definitionCN: 繁荣的；兴旺的

normalIntro.en: Luxuriant carries the idea of too much: plants, hair, and decoration that fill every space.
normalIntro.cn: luxuriant 的核心是「多得过头」：植物、须发与装饰把每一寸空间都填满。

normal.en: Lush plants and luxuriant plants grow thickly, but luxuriant adds a sense of excess.
normal.cn: lush 与 luxuriant 都指长得茂密，但 luxuriant 多一层「过头」的意味。

normal.en: Luxuriant and luxury share the Latin root luxus, meaning excess.
normal.cn: luxuriant 与 luxury 共享拉丁词根 luxus（过度）。

normal.en: Luxuriant vegetation covers the valley after the monsoon.
normal.cn: 季风过后，茂密的植被覆盖了山谷。

normal.en: The suffix -ant makes a describing adjective, as in abundant and elegant.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ant 构成描述性形容词，如 abundant、elegant。

normal.en: Compare luxuriant with luxurious: plants grow luxuriantly, but a hotel is luxurious.
normal.cn: 对比 luxuriant 与 luxurious：植物长得茂盛用前者，酒店豪华用后者。

abstract.en: Picture a forest floor where ferns and vines cover every inch of soil.
abstract.cn: 想象森林地面被蕨类和藤蔓铺满，连一寸泥土都看不见。

abstract.en: Imagine thick hair and a beard so full that they frame the whole face.
abstract.cn: 想象浓密的头发和胡须把整张脸都框住了。

abstract.en: See a palace hall in which gold scrolls cover every wall and ceiling.
abstract.cn: 想象一座宫殿大厅，金色卷草纹铺满每一面墙和天花板。

examples.en: The garden was surrounded by luxuriant tropical plants.
examples.cn: 花园四周是茂盛的热带植物。

examples.en: She has long luxuriant hair that flows past her shoulders.
examples.cn: 她有一头垂到肩下的浓密长发。

examples.en: His letters are full of luxuriant descriptions of the countryside.
examples.cn: 他的书信里满是对乡村风光的华丽描写。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉克修锐安特」——拉开的枝条又密又锐，长满整片地：茂盛、繁复；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 luxus（过度、丰盛）+ luxuria（繁茂）→ luxuriari（疯长、纵情）→ 晚期拉丁语 luxurians → 英语 luxuriant，核心义「长得过盛的丰盈」。

sensesIntro.en: Luxuriant starts with plants that grow too thickly, extends to dense hair and rich decoration, then reaches abundance of thought and prosperity.
sensesIntro.cn: luxuriant 从长得过密的植物出发，扩展到浓密的须发与繁复的装饰，再延伸到思绪的丰沛与地方的繁荣。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: leaves and stems growing so thickly that they hide the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：枝叶密到把地面完全遮住。

branches.en: Plants growing strongly is the basic and most common sense.
branches.cn: 植物疯长是最基本、最常见的义项。

branches.en: Dense hair or foliage uses the same picture of growth without gaps.
branches.cn: 浓密的须发用的也是「密不透风」这幅生长画面。

branches.en: Elaborate design is ornament that has grown like a plant.
branches.cn: 繁复的装饰就像长疯了的花草纹样。

branches.en: Inner richness and public prosperity borrow the image of healthy growth.
branches.cn: 内心的丰富与外在的繁荣都借用了茁壮生长的意象。

branches.en: Colour and sound feel full, while overgrowth hints at criticism.
branches.cn: 颜色与声音显得饱满，而过度的繁盛又带出批评之意。

intro.en: Luxuriant is built on the Latin stem luxus, with the suffix -ant forming an adjective.
intro.cn: luxuriant 建立在拉丁词干 luxus 之上，由后缀 -ant 构成形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin luxus means excess, and luxuriosus means given to excess.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 luxus 意为过度，luxuriosus 意为放纵的。

items.example: Luxus is the root idea of too much.
items.exampleCN: luxus 是「过度」这一词根含义的来源。

items.example: Luxuria covers both plants and pleasure.
items.exampleCN: luxuria 兼指植物的繁茂与感官的放纵。

items.example: Luxuriari gives the image of growth run wild.
items.exampleCN: luxuriari 提供「疯长」的意象。

items.example: The suffix -ant forms adjectives like luxuriant.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 构成 luxuriant 这类形容词。

items.example: Luxuriance names the quality of being luxuriant.
items.exampleCN: luxuriance 指 luxuriant 所具备的性质。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns luxuriant into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把 luxuriant 变成副词。

items.example: Luxury keeps the root sense of excess.
items.exampleCN: luxury 保留词根的「过度」含义。

items.example: Luxurious applies to comfort rather than plants.
items.exampleCN: luxurious 形容舒适奢华，而非植物。

items.meaning: to take great pleasure in something
items.example: Luxuriate keeps the sense of indulging freely.
items.exampleCN: luxuriate 保留纵情享受的含义。

definition_zh: 放大；扩大；夸大；赞美；歌颂
definition_en: to make something look or seem larger, greater, or more important than it is
core_image: 一枚镜头把指尖的细纹放大成整片山坡
scene: 孩子把一片树叶放在放大镜下，叶脉立刻变得又粗又清楚。Under the lens, the leaf veins were magnified until every line showed.
sceneCN: 这里 magnify 是「放大」（第 1 个义项：使物体看起来更大）；句意：在镜片下，叶脉被放大，每条纹路都看得见。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，指放大、放大倍数
由动词加 -er 构成，指放大镜、放大器
同源形容词，指宏伟的、壮丽的
同源名词，指大小、量级

senses.title: To make something look larger
senses.definition: to make an object or image appear bigger than it really is, usually with a lens
senses.definitionCN: 借助镜片等使物体或图像看起来比实际更大
senses.example: The microscope magnifies the cells many times.
senses.exampleCN: 显微镜把细胞放大了许多倍。
senses.why: Latin magnus means great and facere means to make, so magnify is literally to make great in size.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 magnus 意为「大」，facere 意为「使」，所以 magnify 字面就是「使变大」。

senses.title: To increase the size or effect
senses.definition: to make something physically larger or stronger in effect
senses.definitionCN: 使某物在大小或效果上变大、变强
senses.example: A mirror can magnify the light in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 镜子能让房间里的光线变强。
senses.why: The sense of making great extends from sight to any increase in size, strength, or quantity.
senses.whyCN: 「使变大」从视觉延伸到任何大小、强度或数量上的增加。

senses.title: To exaggerate
senses.definition: to make something seem more serious or important than it really is
senses.definitionCN: 使某事显得比实际更严重或更重要
senses.example: Do not magnify a small mistake into a disaster.
senses.exampleCN: 别把小错夸大成灾难。
senses.why: If a lens can make a speck look big, words can do the same to ordinary events, so magnify comes to mean exaggerate.
senses.whyCN: 既然镜片能把一粒灰放大，言语也能把平常小事放大，于是 magnify 有了「夸大」之意。

senses.title: To praise and proclaim
senses.definition: to praise someone or something highly, especially in worship or formal speech
senses.definitionCN: 高度赞扬某人或某物，尤指在礼拜或正式言辞中
senses.example: The choir sang to magnify the name of the Lord.
senses.exampleCN: 唱诗班高唱，赞美主的圣名。
senses.why: To magnify in speech is to make great in words, so the ancient praise sense survives in religious language.
senses.whyCN: 在言语上使人显大，就是在话语中使之伟大，因此古老的「赞颂」义至今留在宗教语言里。

senses.title: To intensify a quality
senses.definition: to make a feeling, difference, or quality stronger and more noticeable
senses.definitionCN: 使情感、差异或某种特质更强烈、更明显
senses.example: The silence only magnified her fear.
senses.exampleCN: 寂静反而加剧了她的恐惧。
senses.why: A magnified image makes details hard to miss, and the same logic makes a feeling that is magnified louder.
senses.whyCN: 被放大的图像让细节无处可藏，同样的道理，被放大的情绪也会更响亮。

senses.title: To widen or spread out
senses.definition: to extend something over a larger area or range
senses.definitionCN: 使某物延伸到更大的范围或面积
senses.example: The plans magnified the map of the old estate.
senses.exampleCN: 这些规划把旧庄园的范围扩展了。
senses.why: The general notion of making great can also mean making wider, which keeps a rare map and survey sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 「使变大」也可以指使范围变宽，这在罕见的地图与测绘用法中仍保留着。

senses.title: To seem larger in the mind
senses.definition: to appear larger or more serious to someone than it actually is
senses.definitionCN: 在某人看来比实际更大或更严重
senses.example: Distances magnify in the dark.
senses.exampleCN: 在黑暗中，距离显得更远。
senses.why: The verb can be used without a lens at all, for the way the mind or the dark makes things seem bigger.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词不必依赖镜片，也能形容心智或黑暗让事物显得更大。

intro.en: Magnify is a Latin compound of magnus, great, and facere, to make.
intro.cn: magnify 是拉丁语复合词，由 magnus（大）与 facere（做、使）结合而成。

items.en: Magnus means great in size, power, or honour.
items.cn: magnus 意为尺寸、力量或荣誉上的「大」。

items.en: Magnificare is the church Latin verb for praising and honouring.
items.cn: magnificare 是教堂拉丁语中「赞美、尊崇」的动词。

items.en: Magnifier carries the word into French with the sense of praising.
items.cn: magnifier 把这个词带入法语，带「颂扬」之意。

items.en: Magnifie appears in English first in the sense of praising or extolling.
items.cn: magnifie 最早在英语中出现时，意为赞美、颂扬。

items.en: With early telescopes and lenses, magnify gains the sense of making things look bigger.
items.cn: 随着早期望远镜与镜片的使用，magnify 获得了「使看起来更大」的含义。

items.en: The praise sense fades, while the optical and exaggerating senses become dominant.
items.cn: 现代英语中赞美义减弱，光学放大与夸大义成为主流。

note.en: Magnify is built on the Latin root magn-, great, and sits close to magnification and magnificent, and to other enlarging words.
note.cn: magnify 建立在拉丁词根 magn-（大）之上，与 magnification、magnificent 同族，也与其它表示「扩大」的词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of making something look bigger
entries.definitionCN: 放大；放大倍数

entries.definition: very impressive and beautiful
entries.definitionCN: 宏伟的；壮丽的，同出 magn- 与 fic 词根

entries.definition: the great size or importance of something
entries.definitionCN: 巨大；重要性；量级

entries.definition: to make something bigger
entries.definitionCN: 扩大；放大

entries.definition: to say something is bigger or worse than it is
entries.definitionCN: 夸大；夸张

entries.definition: to become or make stronger
entries.definitionCN: 加强；强化

normalIntro.en: Magnify joins magn, great, with fy, to make, so it means to make great.
normalIntro.cn: magnify 由 magn（大）与 fy（使……）合成，意思就是「使变大」。

normal.en: The root magn appears in magnificent, magnitude, and magnate.
normal.cn: 词根 magn 可见于 magnificent、magnitude 与 magnate。

normal.en: The suffix -ify means to make, as in simplify and beautify.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ify 意为「使……」，如 simplify、beautify。

normal.en: A magnifying glass makes tiny print readable.
normal.cn: 放大镜让微小的字变得可读。

normal.en: Magnify the problem means to make it seem bigger than it is.
normal.cn: magnify the problem 指把问题说得比实际更严重。

normal.en: Compare magnify with enlarge: magnify often suggests seeing, enlarge suggests size.
normal.cn: 对比 magnify 与 enlarge：前者多与「看」有关，后者侧重体积。

abstract.en: Picture a sunbeam through a lens, burning a bright dot into a paper leaf.
abstract.cn: 想象阳光穿过镜片，在纸叶上烧出一点亮斑。

abstract.en: Imagine a single ant filling the whole window of a microscope.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蚂蚁占满显微镜的整个视野。

abstract.en: See a small worry inflated like a balloon until it fills the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一点小忧虑像气球一样被吹胀，直到塞满整个房间。

examples.en: Strong lenses can magnify an object hundreds of times.
examples.cn: 强透镜能把物体放大数百倍。

examples.en: The newspaper was accused of magnifying the scandal.
examples.cn: 这家报纸被指责夸大了那桩丑闻。

examples.en: Good lighting magnified the colours of the painting.
examples.cn: 良好的灯光让画作的色彩更加鲜明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦格尼坏」——麦子被放大成巨粒，坏了眼神；联想放大镜下的巨大麦粒，记住「放大」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 magnus（大的）+ facere（做、使）→ magnificare（使伟大；赞颂）→ 古法语 magnifier → 英语 magnify，核心义「使变大」。

sensesIntro.en: Magnify begins with making things look bigger, widens to any increase, and then to exaggeration and praise.
sensesIntro.cn: magnify 从「让东西看起来更大」出发，扩展到任何意义上的增大，再延伸出夸大与赞美。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lens that turns a tiny detail into a large, clear shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：镜片把微小的细节放大成清晰的大图。

branches.en: Optical enlargement is the oldest everyday sense.
branches.cn: 光学放大是最日常的义项。

branches.en: Any physical increase makes the object or effect larger.
branches.cn: 任何物理上的增大都让物体或效果变得更大。

branches.en: Exaggeration is enlargement done by words.
branches.cn: 夸大是用语言完成的放大。

branches.en: Praise makes a person great in speech, the historic root of the word.
branches.cn: 赞美在言语中使人显大，这是该词最古老的用法。

branches.en: Intensity, area, and seeming all share the logic of making great.
branches.cn: 强度、范围与观感都共享「使变大」的逻辑。

latinIntro.en: Latin magnus means great, and facere means to make.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 magnus 意为大的，facere 意为做、使。

items.example: The suffix -ication forms the noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ication 构成名词。

items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 表示工具。

items.exampleCN: magnificent 共享 magn- 与 fic 成分。

items.example: Magnitude keeps the plain idea of greatness.

items.example: Magnate also comes from magnus.

definition_zh: 言辞夸张的；夸夸其谈的；浮夸的；自吹自擂的
definition_en: speaking or writing in a grand, lofty way that is often exaggerated
core_image: 一个人站在讲台上张开双臂，把一句平常话吹成大典礼仪
scene: 记者会上，发言人只用空洞的大话描述一件小事，听众越听越不耐烦。At the press conference, the magniloquent speech said nothing about the real problem.
sceneCN: 这里 magniloquent 是「辞藻浮夸、夸夸其谈」（第 1 个义项：用大而无当的言辞说话）；句意：记者会上，那番浮夸的讲话对真正的问题只字未提。

pos.zh: 言辞夸张的；夸夸其谈的
浮华的；过分修饰的（文体）

collocations.zh: 说得天花乱坠却不诚实

由形容词加副词后缀构成，指浮夸地、夸夸其谈地
同构词，由 grandis（宏大）代替 magnus，义为宏大浮夸的

senses.title: Speaking in an exaggerated grand style
senses.titleCN: 言辞夸张的；夸夸其谈的
senses.definition: speaking or writing with words that sound grand but often say little
senses.definitionCN: 说话或写作时用大词、气派十足，却往往内容空洞
senses.example: The magniloquent speaker promised a new world in every sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 那位浮夸的演说者每句话都许诺一个新世界。
senses.why: Latin magnus means great and loqui means to speak, so magniloquent literally means speaking greatly.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 magnus 意为「大」，loqui 意为「说」，所以 magniloquent 字面就是「大话连篇」。

senses.title: Lofty and pompous in tone
senses.definition: showing a high, pompous tone that suits ceremony or self display
senses.definitionCN: 语调高亢、气派，适合典礼场面或自我炫耀
senses.example: His magniloquent tone made a simple request feel like a royal decree.
senses.exampleCN: 他那种浮华的腔调让一个简单的请求听起来像圣旨。
senses.why: The formula echoes grandiloquent and eloquent, so the word describes tone and ceremony rather than content.
senses.whyCN: 这个词与 grandiloquent、eloquent 构词相同，因此多形容腔调与排场，而非内容。

senses.title: Boasting of great achievements
senses.titleCN: 自吹自擂的；大吹大擂的
senses.definition: talking about ones own deeds as if they were much greater than they are
senses.definitionCN: 把自己的功业说得远超实际
senses.example: The general was magniloquent about his victories in every interview.
senses.exampleCN: 这位将军每次受访都对战绩大吹大擂。
senses.why: Making something great in speech turns on the speaker, so the word also points to vanity.
senses.whyCN: 在言语上把事物说大，最终也会反过来指向说话者自己，于是带出自负之意。

senses.title: Persuasive rhetoric without substance
senses.titleCN: 空话连篇的；虚张声势的
senses.definition: using impressive words to persuade while giving no real argument
senses.definitionCN: 用气派十足的语言劝说，却没有真正的论证
senses.example: Many listeners were moved by the speech, but its magniloquent claims were empty.
senses.exampleCN: 许多听众被讲话打动，但其中浮夸的宣称其实空无一物。
senses.why: Because the word is about manner of speaking, it often criticises rhetoric that persuades without truth.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个词重在说话的方式，它常用来批评那种只求说服、不求真实的雄辩。

senses.title: Rich and ornate language
senses.definition: describing language that is rich, elaborate, and full of ornament
senses.definitionCN: 形容语言丰富、繁复、充满修饰
senses.example: The magniloquent prose of the novel is admired by some and mocked by others.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说华美的文笔有人欣赏，也有人嘲弄。
senses.why: Greatness can be felt in colour and ornament, so the word can describe merely rich style without harsh criticism.
senses.whyCN: 「宏大」也可以体现在色彩与修饰上，所以这个词有时只形容文辞华美，并不带强烈贬义。

senses.title: Lofty and elevated in intent
senses.titleCN: 志向高远的；格调高亢的
senses.definition: describing speech that aims at noble and elevated matters
senses.definitionCN: 形容所谈内容指向崇高、高远之事
senses.example: The poem is magniloquent in ambition but simple in form.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗在抱负上高远宏大，形式上却朴素。
senses.why: The same great-speaking formula can praise high aspiration, so the word is not always critical.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「说大话」构词方式也可以用来称许高远抱负，可见这个词并非总是贬义。

senses.title: Sound without meaning in public speech
senses.titleCN: 官腔十足的；空洞浮夸的
senses.definition: describing the inflated language often heard in public announcements or official speeches
senses.definitionCN: 形容公告或官样演说中常见的那种膨胀的空话
senses.example: We grew tired of the magniloquent language in every official notice.
senses.exampleCN: 我们厌倦了每一份官方通告里那种浮夸的官腔。
senses.why: Where ceremony meets routine bureaucracy, the magniloquent style becomes a familiar public target.
senses.whyCN: 当典礼腔与日常官僚公文相遇，浮夸文风就成了人人熟悉的批评对象。

intro.en: Magniloquent is a Latin-style compound of magnus, great, and loqui, to speak, modelled on eloquence.
intro.cn: magniloquent 是拉丁语式的复合词，由 magnus（大）与 loqui（说）构成，仿 eloquent 的构词方式。

items.en: Magnus means great, and loqui means to speak.
items.cn: magnus 意为大的，loqui 意为说话。

items.en: The adjective magniloquus means speaking grandly, first about epic poets such as Virgil.
items.cn: 形容词 magniloquus 意为「说话宏大的」，最早用于描述维吉尔等史诗诗人。

items.en: Court poets used the style to praise rulers in high praise language.
items.cn: 宫廷诗人用这种风格以高调语言颂扬统治者。

items.en: Magniloquent enters English in the seventeenth century as a literary term.
items.cn: 十七世纪 magniloquent 作为文学术语进入英语。

items.en: Critics set magniloquent beside grandiloquent to describe inflated rhetoric.
items.cn: 十八世纪批评家常把 magniloquent 与 grandiloquent 并列，用来形容膨胀的雄辩。

items.en: The word still names speech that claims greatness by the use of grand words alone.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个词仍专指只靠大词自命不凡的言辞。

note.en: Magniloquent is the speaking word built on magn-, great, closely related to grandiloquent and magniloquence, and near to bombastic.
note.cn: magniloquent 是建立在 magn-（大）之上的「说」字，与 grandiloquent、magniloquence 同构，也与 bombastic 语义相近。

entries.definition: using grand words to sound important
entries.definitionCN: 宏词大言的；浮夸的，与 magniloquent 构词相同但词头不同

entries.definition: the quality of speaking grandly
entries.definitionCN: 言辞浮夸；夸张的说话方式

entries.definition: able to speak clearly and well
entries.definitionCN: 雄辩的；有说服力的，与原词共享说辞相关的词尾

entries.definition: using long words to sound important
entries.definitionCN: 夸大浮夸的；辞藻堆砌的

entries.definition: showing too much self importance
entries.definitionCN: 自命不凡的；装腔作势的

entries.definition: trying to appear more important than is true
entries.definitionCN: 自命不凡的；做作的

normalIntro.en: Magniloquent joins magn, great, with loqu, to speak, so it describes speaking in a grand way.
normalIntro.cn: magniloquent 把 magn（大）与 loqu（说）拼在一起，形容说话摆出宏大的架势。

normal.en: The root loqu appears in eloquent, loquacious, and soliloquy.
normal.cn: 词根 loqu 可见于 eloquent、loquacious 与 soliloquy。

normal.en: Grandiloquent swaps magn for grand but means almost the same thing.
normal.cn: grandiloquent 把 magn 换成 grand，意思几乎相同。

normal.en: A magniloquent speech impresses at first and bores after a while.
normal.cn: 浮夸的演讲初听惊人，听久了就乏味。

normal.en: The suffix -quent comes from Latin loqui and marks speaking words.
normal.cn: 后缀 -quent 源自拉丁语 loqui，标记与说话有关的词。

normal.en: Compare magniloquent with eloquent: eloquent moves you, magniloquent inflates.
normal.cn: 对比 magniloquent 与 eloquent：前者膨胀，后者动人。

abstract.en: Picture a speaker on a stage whose words rise like balloons, light and empty.
abstract.cn: 想象一位讲台上的演说者，话像气球一样越升越高，轻而无物。

abstract.en: Imagine one plain sentence wearing a giant robe and a crown.
abstract.cn: 想象一句平白的话穿上了巨大的长袍、戴上了王冠。

abstract.en: See a microphone that turns every whisper into a royal fanfare.
abstract.cn: 想象一支麦克风把每句低语都放大成皇室号角。

examples.en: His magniloquent acceptance speech lasted almost an hour.
examples.cn: 他那番浮夸的获奖致辞持续了将近一小时。

examples.en: Critics praised the novel but found its magniloquent style heavy.
examples.cn: 评论家称赞这部小说，却觉得它文风浮夸沉重。

examples.en: The magniloquent promises of the campaign were soon forgotten.
examples.cn: 竞选时那些夸夸其谈的承诺很快就被遗忘了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦克尼罗夸」——麦克风前把话夸得又大又响：夸夸其谈；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 magnus（大）+ loqui（说）→ 拉丁语 magniloquus（说大话的）→ 英语 magniloquent，核心义「把话往大了说」。

sensesIntro.en: Magniloquent begins with speech that sounds grand, then covers pompous tone, boasting, empty rhetoric, and sometimes noble ambition.
sensesIntro.cn: magniloquent 先用来说听起来宏大的言辞，进而涵盖浮华的腔调、自吹、空洞的雄辩，有时也指高远的抱负。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plain sentence dressed up in a giant ceremonial robe.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句平常的话被套上巨大的礼服。

branches.en: Exaggerated grand speech is the central sense.
branches.cn: 夸张宏大的言辞是核心义项。

branches.en: The pompous tone is the ceremonial side of the word.
branches.cn: 高亢浮华的腔调是这个词的典礼面向。

branches.en: Boasting turns the great words on the speaker himself.
branches.cn: 自吹把大话转而指向说话者自己。

branches.en: Empty rhetoric and official language show the word at its most critical.
branches.cn: 空洞的雄辩与官腔体现了这个词最强烈的批评色彩。

branches.en: Ornate style and lofty ambition remind us the word can sometimes admire.
branches.cn: 华美文体与高远抱负提醒我们，这个词有时也能表示赞赏。

intro.en: Magniloquent is built from two Latin stems, magn, great, and loqu, speak, with the suffix -ent.
intro.cn: magniloquent 由 magn（大）、loqu（说）两个拉丁词干加后缀 -ent 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin magnus means great, and loqui means to speak.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 magnus 意为大的，loqui 意为说话。

items.exampleCN: 词根 magn- 提供「大」的含义。

items.example: The root loqu- appears in eloquent and loquacious.
items.exampleCN: 词根 loqu- 见于 eloquent 与 loquacious。

items.example: The suffix -ent forms adjectives such as magniloquent.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ent 构成 magniloquent 这类形容词。

items.example: Magniloquus is the direct Latin model.
items.exampleCN: magniloquus 是直接的拉丁语范本。

items.example: The suffix -ence makes the noun of quality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ence 构成性质名词。

items.example: Grandiloquent uses grand instead of magn.
items.exampleCN: grandiloquent 用 grand 代替 magn。

items.example: Eloquent shares the speaking root loqu-.
items.exampleCN: eloquent 共享表示「说」的词根 loqu-。

items.example: Somniloquent combines sleep with speech.
items.exampleCN: somniloquent 把睡眠与说话组合起来。

items.meaning: a person who makes a voice seem to come from elsewhere
items.example: Ventriloquist keeps the loqu- speaking stem.
items.exampleCN: ventriloquist 保留 loqu- 这个「说」的词干。
